wave1.headline: Credit-fund flows (CVM inf_diario) and fund holdings (CDA) are clearly visible but do not beat P4+Q. Flows follow returns rather than lead them, so flow-timing overlays lose 0.06–0.54%/yr. The only real cross-sectional effect, fire-sale pressure, is gone within about a month and costs erase it. The best variant, dropping bonds held by few credit funds, adds +0.08%/yr (t 0.86, Holm p=1) and is flat in the 2026 holdout.
wave1.best: X4_ex_low_credit_share: P4+Q minus the bottom quintile of cshare (share of a bond's fund-held value owned by PIT credit funds), monthly decisions, 126-bday tranches
insights: Flows follow returns: the 21d credit-fund flow correlates +0.41 with P4+Q's previous-month return (+0.60 for IDA-DI). In a regression of next-month return on flow plus own lagged return, flow is never significant (t 0.6 for af21, 1.4 for af5, 0.07 for af63).

The 2023 wave took out about 5.5% of credit-fund PL per month. It began after the Americanas event (Feb 2023) and ended (net inflows again from about Aug 2023) while the universe median spread was still near its 200 bps peak. Flow overlays therefore exit late and re-enter late: in P4+Q if af21>0 is -0.47%/yr (t -1.2), af63>0 is -0.54 (t -1.7), and out if af21<-2% is -0.06 pre-2026 and -1.89 (t -3.1) in the 2026 holdout.

Fire-sale pressure (holders' 21d outflow weighted by holding) is real but lasts about a month. Dropping the bottom quintile adds +0.32%/yr vs P4+Q at a 1-month cohort horizon (t 2.3), -0.03 at 3m and -0.11 at 6m, which fits Coval-Stafford pressure followed by reversal. Harvesting it with weekly 21d tranches means about 14x turnover: -0.11 at 25bps and -0.26 at 50bps (t -2.1).

'Orphan' debentures that no investment fund holds are 6% of the universe and 9% of P4+Q, and they outperform. Removing them costs -0.16%/yr (t -2.4; 6m cohort t -3.5), and this survives the rec40 scenario. Their raw fwd_126 is 2.0% vs 1.15% for held bonds, with lower carry (110 vs 118 bps). This looks like a neglect premium, but these are the stale-mark/survivorship names.

Credit-fund ownership share is a carry proxy. Within DI-spread bonds its 3m IC is +0.13 (t 5.4), but carry-neutral it is +0.01 (t 0.8). P4+Q already captures it, so all three cshare book variants (X4, F3, X7) land at +0.01 to +0.08.
Funds' net buying (CDA buys-sells), changes in holder count and quantity, and holder concentration carry no information (|IC| <= 0.03, insignificant raw or carry-neutral).

Structural boom: debenture-heavy funds (>=25% of PL) grew from 597 to 2,005 and from about R$0.25tn to R$1.1tn PL (2022-01 to 2025-12), and CDA debenture positions per month grew from 44k to over 200k. Credit-fund investor counts fell 14% in Q1 2026, the redemption wave that is now in the holdout.
signals: press21 / press63: holding-weighted holder net flow, a short-horizon (<=1 month) fire-sale avoid signal. Load with features.signals(panel) in research/nightly/fund_flows/features.py or from data/history/nightly/fund_flows/bond_signals_M.pkl.
stress63: share of a bond's fund holders with 63d outflows above 10% (same sources)
nh / lnh: number of fund holders; nh==0 flags 'orphan' bonds, a candidate positive tilt pending a survivorship check (same sources)
cshare, hhi, dnh3, dq3, nb3: ownership structure and fund net trading, which showed no alpha (same sources)

af21 / af63 / dcot63: aggregate credit-fund flow regime, usable as a descriptor or conditioning variable but not as a timing rule. Load with features.agg_flows() or data/history/nightly/fund_flows/agg_flows_export.pkl.
features.fund_class(): PIT credit-fund classification per CDA month; features.fund_flow_ratios(W): per-fund flow ratios (not lagged; shift 5 days before use)
caveats: CVM rewrites CDA files: 2023 data was regenerated in 2024, so it may include positions that were confidential or filed late at the time. The 60-day availability lag mitigates this but does not remove it, and the most recent vintages are visibly incomplete (2026-07 has 1,272 credit funds vs about 2,300).

Flows are measured at the funds that directly hold debentures (masters). Feeder (FIC) flows only reach them through master subscriptions and redemptions. Mergers and incorporations create spikes: fund flow ratios are clipped to +/-100% and funds with PL below R$5m are ignored.
Harness caveats apply: smooth, stale marks inflate t and Sharpe. The orphan effect sits in the stale-mark/survivorship zone, even though it survives rec40.
Overlays switch instantly at the mark (optimistic) and still lose.

problems: The CDA holdings use a 60-day lag, but CVM keeps positions confidential for about 90 days. I used the 2026-07 file as downloaded on 2026-09-28, about 60 days after month-end. Its debenture positions (BLC_4) show only R$310bn by bond. Another R$500bn (2,520 funds, about 62% of value) sits in cda_fi_CONFID_202607.csv with no bond code; the confidentiality end dates (DT_CONFID_APLIC) run from 2026-10-29 to 2027-01-27. By comparison, 2026-04 (about 150 days old) shows R$767bn visible and only R$0.7bn still confidential. build_data.py reads only BLC_4 from files CVM has already regenerated. So the backtest's 60-day vintages include positions that were hidden in real time. This is look-ahead: the README calls it a mitigated caveat, but it is a real leak.

With a realistic lag, X4's edge shrinks steadily. vs P4+Q it is +0.083 (t 0.86) at 60 days, reproduced exactly; +0.032 (t 0.43) at 90; +0.013 (t 0.23) at 120; and -0.035 (t -0.66) at 180. At 50 bps it is +0.006 at 120 days. The 2022–23 half is negative at every lag.

The orphan insight (X5, about -0.16%/yr, t -2.4, 'survives rec40') is weaker than stated and also depends on the lag. It is -0.12 (t -1.5) at 120 days and -0.05 (t -0.37) at 180. The 'orphan' flag is also polluted by newly issued bonds whose holdings have no vintage yet: the orphan share grows from 5.9% at a 60-day lag to 16.6% at 180. It is not a clean neglect premium.

X4's +0.08%/yr reproduces exactly (t 0.86; 50 bps +0.078), but it is not robust. Removing the 5 issuers whose exclusion helped most gives +0.005 (t 0.07), and removing the top 10 gives -0.012. One issuer (cnpj8 12104241, only 5 excluded obs) contributes about -1.5 of summed relative fwd_126, so X4 mostly dodged one or two blow-ups.
Excluding the 3 best months of X4 vs P4+Q leaves -0.015%/yr (excluding the best one leaves +0.05). By year: 2022 +0.02, 2023 -0.18, 2024 +0.33, 2025 +0.16, so the gain is concentrated in 2024.

X4 is sensitive to parameters. Quintile cut: q=0.10 gives +0.01, 0.15 gives +0.02, 0.25 gives +0.11, 0.30 gives +0.17 (t 1.4), 0.40 gives +0.16. Holding period: 63d gives +0.14, 252d gives -0.01, quarterly rebalance gives +0.04. Credit-fund threshold: 10% gives -0.00, 50% gives +0.04, 75% gives +0.07. All are insignificant, and the sign flips in several cells.

wave1.headline: None of the 20 macro or credit-cycle timing and sizing overlays beats P4+Q before 2026; macro-to-credit links flip sign between 2010–21 and 2022–25, and switching costs eat what timing skill is left.
wave1.best: ov_mom63_inout: IDA-DI 63-day excess momentum > 0, in or out, checked at each Friday close and applied to the whole P4+Q book. It came out +0.02%/yr vs P4+Q (t 0.05, Holm p 1.0) and cut maxDD from −1.39% to −0.50%. It then lost 1.04%/yr vs P4+Q in the 2026 holdout (t −2.28).
insights: Macro signals flip sign across regimes. Non-overlapping monthly Spearman correlation with IDA-DI's forward 21d excess, 2010–21 vs 2022–25: VIX level +0.18 vs −0.34; Brazil country-risk proxy +0.10 vs −0.37; USD/BRL 63d −0.23 vs +0.20; EMB/IEF +0.24 vs −0.10; IDA-DI vol63 +0.43 vs −0.12. Only the index's own momentum (x5 +0.43/+0.44, x21 +0.40/+0.36), Brent 63d (+0.24/+0.32) and US HY via HYG/IEF (+0.32/+0.18) keep their sign. As a result the walk-forward ridge and GBM, trained on 2010–21, have timing alpha of −1.6 to −2.2%/yr (t −3.7 to −3.9) against an exposure-matched static book.

The pre-declared primary, an ensemble sizing 0–1.5× (logit + ridge + GBM + HMM + mom21), lost 0.97%/yr vs P4+Q (t −2.7), and 2.11%/yr at 50 bps. In the 2026 holdout it lost 0.12%/yr vs P4+Q. Continuous sizing makes 13–27 switches a year, which costs 0.5–2%/yr; every 'size' variant is worse than in/out.

The current P4 regime overlay (IDA21) costs 0.48%/yr on P4+Q (1.19%/yr at 50 bps). Its exposure-matched timing alpha is −0.01, so the loss comes from lower average exposure (0.79) plus costs. It does beat random timing: 200 circular shifts average −1.15, p = 0.00.

Slow momentum is the only rule that works on the long IDA-DI sample. Over 2012–21 out of sample, mom63 in/out had Sharpe 1.61 vs 0.39 buy-and-hold and maxDD −0.83% vs −5.9%, with 1.2 switches a year. On P4+Q it had timing alpha +0.51 (t 1.8), vol 0.82 vs 1.04 and maxDD −0.50 vs −1.39. But almost all of its gain vs P4+Q came from one episode (Americanas, Jan–Feb 2023), and it lost 1.04%/yr in the 2026 holdout. Treat it as drawdown insurance with one good episode, not alpha.

The implementable version scales only NEW monthly tranches with no forced selling. This removes most of the cost damage: entry_ens_size and entry_gbm_size came out −0.10%/yr vs P4+Q with timing alpha +0.13 to +0.19 (t < 0.8). It is the right way to express a macro view in an illiquid book, but there is no view worth expressing.

Leaning into wide spreads did not pay. Sizing up when the universe's median CDI+ spread is high (expanding z-score) lost 1.09%/yr as an overlay and 0.63%/yr at entry; carry-level timing alpha was about 0.

Static leverage is the only thing that 'beats' P4+Q, and it is carry scaling, not skill. With funding at CDI + 50 bps, 1.25× gave +0.44%/yr (t 2.5) and 1.5× gave +0.88%/yr, but maxDD grew to −1.78% and −2.16%. This depends entirely on repo funding for debentures near CDI + 50, which is not realistic for most HY names.

Debenture primary issuance (CVM registrations, 91d, year-on-year) and IPCA surprises vs the Focus survey show no timing value: correlations stay within about 0.04 in both periods, except issuance yoy at +0.15 in 2022–25.
Adding a 5–10 day extra lag makes IDA21 a further 0.08–0.24%/yr worse. Part of the momentum edge is autocorrelation from smooth, stale marks, which a real illiquid book cannot trade at those marks.
signals: macro_overlay_signals.pkl (data/history/nightly/macro_cycle/): date index; columns ens_size, ens_inout, gbm_size, hmm_inout, logit_inout, spread_size, ens_pct. Each is a book-level exposure known at the close of that date. Pass it to harness.backtest(overlay=series).
research/nightly/macro_cycle/data.py:build(): the point-in-time macro panel (market-level features for any combiner; join on date <= decision day).
research/nightly/macro_cycle/run.py:apply_overlay(base_result, exposure_series, cost_bps, fund_bps, extra_lag): the harness overlay semantics plus funding on the levered part.
research/nightly/macro_cycle/run.py:entry_sized(signal, exposure_series): scales only new 126d tranches; the implementable way to apply an exposure.
IDA-DI 63d excess momentum (macro_daily.pkl column IDADI_x63 > 0): a slow drawdown-control flag.
caveats: Only about 2 credit episodes fall in the 48 pre-2026 months (Americanas in Q1-2023 and late 2025). The long IDA-DI sample (2012–21) adds 2015–16 and 2020, but that is the index, not the book.
The ov_* overlays (including the harness IDA21 regime) switch the whole book instantly at the mark, which is optimistic for illiquid debentures. The entry_* variants are the implementable ones.
Smooth, stale marks inflate Sharpe and t, and momentum rules partly exploit their autocorrelation.
Funding for leverage at CDI + 50 bps (100 bps as a sensitivity) is an assumption; no debenture repo market was modelled.

problems: net50_diff_vs_p4q_ann_pct = -0.2 in the claimed metrics does not appear anywhere in results.json, because mom63 is missing from the robustness keys. When I recomputed it, 50 bps with a 50 bps base gave -0.06%/yr (t -0.16). The number is misreported, although the conclusion (about zero) still holds.

The circular-shift placebo was never run for the chosen best variant (mom63). I ran it: 200 shifts give a mean of -0.64 and a p95 of -0.34, against an actual +0.02 (p = 0.02). So mom63 has real timing information compared with random timing, but it adds nothing over always-invested P4+Q.

The best variant is a selection artifact. Neighbouring momentum windows on the same overlay all do worse vs P4+Q: 21d -0.50, 84d -0.31, 126d -0.52. Only 42d (+0.02) is about the same. The +0.02 is the maximum of 17 non-static variants and should be read as 0.
My reproduction matches ov_mom63_inout exactly at 25 bps: +0.018%/yr vs P4+Q (NW t 0.05), halves +0.39 / −0.35, vol 0.82, maxDD −0.50. It adds nothing over P4+Q, which is what the agent claims.

The headline's net50 figure of −0.20%/yr has no source in the agent's code. mom63 is not in run.py's robustness list, so it was never computed at 50 bps there. I re-ran it at 50 bps (with the 50 bps baseline) and got −0.06%/yr (t −0.16). The conclusion is the same but the number is wrong.

The value comes from one episode, and the months differ from the README. The biggest gains are Feb and Mar 2023 (+0.62% and +0.31%), not Jan–Feb as the README says; Jan 2023 is slightly negative (−0.06%). Excluding Jan–Mar 2023 gives −0.21%/yr (t −0.74). Excluding all of 2023 gives −0.24%/yr. Dropping the 5 best months gives −0.47%/yr (t −1.35). Jan–Mar 2025 alone cost about −1.5% cumulative.

wave1.headline: Among 110 point-in-time factors, only a small composite led by equity momentum and volatility adds to P4+Q, and only as a screen inside the top-carry bucket. Dropping the worst 20% of P4+Q names by the composite adds +0.36%/yr (NW t 2.5, positive in both halves, placebo p≈0), but that is not significant after Holm (p 0.13), and the gain shrank to +0.12%/yr (t 1.3) in the 9-month 2026 holdout.
wave1.best: zoo_screen20: P4+Q minus the worst 20% (within P4+Q) of an equal-weight normal-score composite of 8 survivors chosen on 2021-03..2023-06 data: ds_5(-), days_since_distress(-), eq_r21(+), eq_r126(+), bond_age_y(+), dres_21(-), age/days_since_trade(+), eq_vol63(-)
insights: Equity momentum is the only factor block that is clearly incremental. Holding carry, RV, duration, IPCA and incentivada fixed, eq_r126 has a 6m IC of +0.107 (NW t 6.8), +0.117 in the 2024-25 validation period and +0.18 inside P4+Q (t 7.4). Its raw IC is only about 0.04, so it is invisible without conditioning on carry. The equity-only sub-composite delivers +0.29 of the +0.36%/yr.
eq_vol63 works as a risk flag and is orthogonal to momentum (a separate cluster). Its IC after controls is -0.09 at 6m and -0.14 at 12m.

Short-horizon mark momentum: a spread that widened over the last week (ds_5) predicts 6-12m underperformance (IC after controls -0.048, t -5.5), and so does a rising residual over 21 days (dres_21, -0.036). Spread momentum over 63-252 days is about 0 once carry is controlled. This looks like slow price discovery in stale marks. As a screen it adds only +0.09 to +0.12%/yr.

Decay rises with horizon for nearly every survivor. For eq_r126 the IC after controls is 0.03/0.07/0.11/0.13 at 21/63/126/252 bdays; for eq_vol63 it is -0.02/-0.05/-0.09/-0.14. These are slow credit-drift factors, which is consistent with 'reacting fast doesn't pay'.

Many factors look strong in raw IC but vanish after carry and RV. Residual smoothings (rz_ma5/21, resid_bps) have a raw IC of +0.21 (t 11) but only 0.03-0.06 after controls. The issuer-average residual goes from a raw IC of +0.18 to -0.01. Liquidity (Amihud, volume, trade counts), guarantee type, 476 vs 400 offerings, call clause, coupon frequency and issue size have |t| < 2 or flip sign across periods.

Several selection-period winners flipped sign in validation: days_since_distress (t -7.5, then IC +0.04), bond_age_y (t +3.5, then -0.01) and is_476 (t +4.5, then -3.7). A 2.5-year selection window picks up regime artefacts.

Carry cannot be replaced. Tilting the carry rank with the composite loses -0.11%/yr vs P4+Q. The composite only helps as a screen inside the top-30% carry bucket, and without the fundamentals quality screen (P4 minus the composite) the gain falls to +0.11. Quality and the zoo composite are complementary.

zoo_screen20 before 2026: 2.58%/yr over CDI, +1.47 vs universe (t 2.9), +0.36 vs P4+Q (t 2.54; +0.32 in 2022-23 and +0.39 in 2024-25), vol 0.88, max drawdown -0.77%, 82 names. Robustness vs P4+Q: 50 bps +0.33 (t 2.3), rec40 +0.36, hold 63 +0.43, weekly tranches +0.40 (t 2.7). A placebo that drops 20% of P4+Q at random gives a mean of -0.04 and a p95 of +0.01.
Sealed holdout, 2026-01..09: +0.20%/yr over CDI, +0.12 vs P4+Q (t 1.3, ahead in 8 of 9 months) and +3.46 vs universe (t 4.2).
signals: zoo composite: research/nightly/factor_zoo/features.py::signals(panel) returns (day, codigo, value), higher is better, with the spec frozen in results.json 'composite_spec'. The cached version is data/history/nightly/factor_zoo/zoo_composite.pkl with columns day, codigo, cnpj8, value, freq M|W, covering universe rows through 2026-09.

all zoo features: features.py::build_features() returns (day, codigo, ~60 features); features.py::attach(panel) merges them into a harness panel and adds is_ipca, eq_idio63, eq_mom_12_1, eq_vol_trend, rat_down_365, ds_63_vs_peer, sec_ds_63, sec_resid.

Most robust single overlays: eq_r126(+), eq_r21(+) and eq_vol63(-), which are harness panel columns, and ds_5(-) (1-week CDI+ spread change) from features.py. Use them as a bottom-20% screen inside P4+Q.
caveats: After Holm across the 11 variants tried (plus P4), the result is not significant: p 0.13 for the best variant, raw p 0.011. In the 9-month holdout the increment shrank to +0.12%/yr, t 1.3.

Survivors were chosen from only 28 monthly dates, and 4 of the 8 were unstable in validation (days_since_distress, bond_age_y, age, and also is_476 among the candidates). The equity block is the only robust part.
Smooth and stale marks inflate the t-stats and Sharpe ratios. The 'age' (days since last trade) survivor may be partly a mark-staleness artefact.
SND registry fields come from a 2026-09 snapshot, so repactuated bonds carry their current terms. Outstanding-quantity and redemption fields were deliberately excluded because they are look-ahead.

problems: days_since_distress uses a 9999 sentinel for 'never distressed'. That covers at least 50% of universe rows (the median is 9999). With sign -1, the composite gives recently distressed issuers a positive score and puts the tied sentinel mass in the middle. The 'single_days_since_distress_screen20' variant (16 names, +0.30) is a bug artefact: its bottom 20% quantile falls on the tied value, so it drops nearly all P4+Q names and keeps only the recently distressed ones. The claim that it 'flips sign' is also partly a tie artefact. Removing the factor from the composite gives +0.31%/yr (t 2.3) instead of +0.36.

The 2022-23 half is not out-of-sample. Survivors were picked on decisions from 2021-03 to 2023-06, which overlap the 2022-23 book. Within that window the diff is +0.32 (t 1.24). The truly out-of-selection months, 2024-25, give +0.39 (t 3.4), so evidence outside the selection window does exist. But 'positive in both halves' overstates it, because one half is in-sample.

The signal decays quickly, which contradicts the insight that these are 'slow credit-drift factors'. Using the composite from the previous monthly decision (information one month staler) roughly halves the increment, to +0.18%/yr (t 1.6). A good part of the gain comes from the fresh short-horizon components (ds_5, dres_21, eq_r21). This is not leakage: entry is strictly at a trade after the decision close.

The gain comes from a few issuer blowups. Excluding the top 2 avoided issuers (00776574, the Americanas CNPJ, in Jan 2023 and 12104241, a listed healthcare name, in late 2024) cuts the gain to +0.21%/yr (t 2.2). Excluding the top 3 gives +0.16 (t 1.4), the top 5 +0.12 (t 1.1) and the top 10 +0.04 (t 0.5). Excluding the top 5 or 10 kept winners changes nothing (+0.35).
Three months (2024-12, 2023-01, 2024-04) drive the result. Without them the gain is +0.13%/yr (t 1.2).

'Positive in both halves' is partly in-sample. The survivors were chosen on decisions from 2021-03 to 2023-06, whose 6m labels overlap most of the 2022-23 half, including Americanas. The clean out-of-sample window (decisions from 2023-07, P&L 2024-25) gives +0.39 (t 3.4). Removing the single issuer 12104241 makes it +0.23 (t 1.8), and excluding the top 3 makes it +0.11 (t 0.8).

wave1.headline: None of the 51 model variants tried (9 learners plus 2 ensembles plus 2 non-ML controls, 4 portfolio forms each) beats P4+Q after multiple-testing correction. The best one tilts P4+Q weights using a LightGBM model trained on each bond's excess over its peer group: it adds +0.17%/yr pre-2026 (t 2.2, Holm p 1.0, all of it in 2024–25) and +0.11%/yr in the sealed 2026 holdout. On their own, all the ML rankers lose 0.5–1.5%/yr to P4+Q, and none ranks bonds better than carry (cdi_bps) or the richness measure resid_z.
wave1.best: lgb_peer:tilt (P4+Q with weights proportional to 0.5 + the percentile of a LightGBM score whose target is fwd_126 minus the same-date peer-group mean; walk-forward, embargo 126 bdays, 25 bps)
insights: The raw-target models (LGBM, monotone LGBM, elastic net, hierarchical shrinkage, CatBoost) have universe IC of about 0 (-0.05 to +0.07). Trained on 2021 labels, they learned 'low carry is good' and posted ICs of -0.4 to -0.65 from 2022-03 to 2022-10, when carry alone had +0.6 to +0.7. Demeaning the target within the peer group (lgb_peer) fixes this: IC 0.16, NW t 4.8, the only model positive in every sub-period. The lesson is to predict within-peer excess, not raw return, because the ranking across peer groups is regime-driven and flips sign.

No model matches single raw columns. cdi_bps has IC 0.25 in the universe and 0.33 inside P4+Q (t 11.2). resid_z has IC 0.23 with NW t 14.6, the most stable signal. The best model inside P4+Q reaches 0.25.

As overlays inside P4+Q the models are weakly positive: lgb_peer:tilt +0.17 (t 2.18), stack:tilt +0.16, stack:veto20 +0.15 (t 2.89, Holm 0.18), lgb_peer:veto20 +0.12. The tilt also holds at 50 bps (+0.17), under rec40 (+0.17), at hold 63 (+0.23) and at cohort level (+0.14, t 1.9). It beats all 30 random-tilt placebos (placebo p95 +0.06). But the gain is +0.01 in 2022–23 and +0.33 in 2024–25.

The one Holm-significant result is a trivial non-ML control. Tilting P4+Q weights by carry percentile (ctrl_carry:tilt) gives +0.06%/yr with t 5.22 and Holm p < 0.001. The size is tiny and the t is inflated by a very low tracking error, but it is a free refinement for a combiner.
As standalone top-20% books every ML model loses to P4+Q, by -0.5 (lgb_peer) to -1.5%/yr, mostly in 2022–23 (-1.5 to -2.9). This confirms the earlier deep lab.
The large-loss classifier (P(fwd_126 < -3%), about 7% base rate) is useless as a veto. Its IC is about 0 and changes sign by year. As a veto it adds +0.08 (t 1.4), entirely in 2022–23.

Learning-to-rank objectives (LightGBM LambdaRank, XGBoost pairwise, CatBoost YetiRank) are no better than L2 regression as overlays (within ±0.05%/yr). They optimise the top of the list, while an overlay needs the full ordering inside P4+Q. Monotone constraints change nothing. Hierarchical issuer and sector shrinkage on past residuals hurts (IC inside P4+Q 0.09), so past issuer alpha does not persist.
NNLS stacking on past out-of-sample predictions converges to 92% lgb_peer and 8% lgb_rank by 2025-12.

SHAP of lgb_peer (fit 2025-10, 2025 out-of-sample rows): the top drivers are carry x duration, carry vs the kind median, equity drawdown vs its 252d high (a smaller drawdown raises the score), years to maturity, raw carry, duration, IDA-DI 63d momentum, carry vs sector, fundamental quality (+), equity 252d return (+) and equity vol (-). In short: carry within peers, adjusted for duration, plus the issuer's equity health.
Sealed holdout, looked at once with the variant frozen (2026-01 to 2026-09): lgb_peer:tilt +0.11%/yr vs P4+Q (t 1.2, 7 of 9 months positive). Excess over CDI was +0.19 vs +0.08 for P4+Q.
signals: ml_lgb_peer_pct: walk-forward per-date percentile of the LightGBM peer-excess model (best). Load with research/nightly/ml_ranking/run.py::signals(panel=None, name='ml_lgb_peer_pct'), which returns (codigo, cnpj8, date, value); monthly dates 2022-01..2025-12, known at the close of date.
ml_stack_pct, ml_ens_pct, ml_lgb_rank_pct, ml_hier_pct, ml_lgb_loss_pct (higher = safer): same function and cache, data/history/nightly/ml_ranking/signals_ml_ranking.pkl
Raw walk-forward predictions per model: data/history/nightly/ml_ranking/pred_<model>.pkl (keys pred [day,dpos,codigo,cnpj8,pred,fit_pos] and params)

ctrl_carry tilt: P4+Q weights proportional to 0.5 + the cdi_bps percentile (non-ML, +0.06%/yr, t 5.2); defined in run.py stage_eval together with overlay_signals()
caveats: Smooth, stale debenture marks inflate every t-stat, especially paired t-stats at tracking errors around 0.1%/yr (the carry tilt's t of 5.2). The ML overlay gains appear only in 2024–25.
The best variant is the maximum of 51 pre-2026 results, so its Holm p is 1.0. The 9-month holdout agrees in sign (+0.11) but is not significant.
The first models (2022) train on only 5 to 10 labelled monthly dates, which drives the 2022 inversion of the raw-target models.

The compute budget was cut on the shared machine (LightGBM with 2 threads ran 3x slower than with 1): one nested optuna tuning point (2024-01) with 6 trials, reused for 2025; 2022–23 on defaults; CatBoost YetiRank on defaults only; refits every 6 months instead of monthly.

problems: No leakage found. The claim reproduces exactly from the cached walk-forward predictions: lgb_peer:tilt vs P4+Q is +0.1716%/yr, NW t 2.18, 2022-23 +0.01, 2024-25 +0.33 (script verify_leakage/v1_repro.py).

Embargo check: every training row satisfies lab_end_126 <= fit_pos <= decision dpos, but with zero slack. The label is realised at the close of the refit day and used at that same close. This is valid, yet the margin is thin. Adding an extra embargo of 21 bdays gives +0.169 (t 2.09). Adding 63 bdays gives +0.138 (t 1.92), with 2022-23 turning negative (-0.02). The veto20 form roughly halves under the 63-bday embargo (+0.12 to +0.07).

One residual look-ahead remains in the shared harness: spike cleaning (ratio_c) uses the next trade, so it feeds the R-derived path features. Dropping all 11 R-derived features (br_*, bvol, bstale, bmdd, bmin, iss_br*, sec_br63, iss_worst_bmdd) leaves the tilt unchanged at +0.173 (t 2.08). This channel does not drive the result.

Concentration: 5 issuers produce 58% of the tilt's cohort-level gain (cnpj8 12104241, 12647827, 61486650, 12979552, 09074183). Dropping the top-5 contributing issuers from both books cuts the gain from +0.17 to +0.07%/yr (t 1.47). Dropping the top 10 cuts it to +0.05 (t 1.04). This exclusion is selected in-sample, so it is a harsh test, but it shows the edge is not broad.

Time concentration: +0.01 in 2022-23, +0.54 in 2024 (t 5.1, 12/12 months positive), +0.12 in 2025 (t 1.7). Five of the top 6 months are in 2024 or 2025. Removing the best 3 months leaves +0.11 (t 1.99). Excluding 2023 or the 2023H1 crisis actually helps (+0.23 / +0.19), so this is not a crisis artefact. It is a single-year effect.

The ML adds little over one-line non-ML tilts. Paired against the tilted-carry control the ML tilt is +0.11 (t 1.41). Against carry x duration it is +0.07 (t 2.05); against carry vs kind median +0.08 (t 1.41); against carry vs peer median +0.10 (t 1.40); against resid_z +0.10 (t 1.17); against peer-carry+resid +0.10 (t 1.31). None of these survives any multiplicity correction. The non-ML tilts earn +0.06 to +0.10 vs P4+Q with higher t (2.9-5.2).

wave1.headline: Dropping the P4+Q names with the worst equity-implied credit risk adds about +0.35%/yr vs P4+Q (t 1.65) and nearly halves max drawdown, but this is not significant after Holm correction, and a plain 52-week equity-drawdown filter does just as well as the Merton/CreditGrades models.
wave1.best: A3_P4Q_avoid_CGworstQ: P4+Q minus the worst quintile (per date, among universe rows with a signal) of the CreditGrades 5-year equity-implied spread. A1, which removes the worst Merton distance-to-default quintile instead, is almost identical.
insights: Raw distance to default has no predictive power (IC -0.035) because it mostly stands in for carry. Once carry is held fixed it does predict: partial IC +0.054 (t 5.1) for 6-month returns. Carry only partly pays for the risk the equity market signals.

Avoid rules inside P4+Q, pre-2026: removing the worst CreditGrades quintile gives +0.35%/yr vs P4+Q (t 1.65), and removing the worst distance-to-default quintile gives +0.34 (t 1.62). Both halves are positive (+0.17 in 2022-23, +0.53 in 2024-25). Volatility falls from 1.00 to 0.93 and max drawdown from -1.32% to -0.74%. The result holds at 50 bps (+0.34) and under the 40%-recovery scenario (+0.34). The removed names earned 0.92% less over 6 months than the kept names (t 2.0).

Random-exclusion placebo (the same number of listed P4+Q names dropped at random, 20 draws): mean +0.14, 95th percentile +0.19. The actual +0.35 beats all 20. Part of the placebo gain comes from tilting the book toward unlisted names.

The structural model adds almost nothing over simple equity measures. Removing the worst 52-week equity drawdown quintile gives +0.34 (t 1.84, Holm 0.72), and removing the worst 63-day equity volatility quintile gives +0.29. Their Spearman correlations with distance to default are 0.60 and -0.87. Market leverage alone has zero IC.

Distance to default complements the fundamentals quality filter rather than replacing it. Using it instead of that filter (P4 minus the worst distance-to-default quintile) is +0.12 below... correction: +0.12 above P4 minus quality baseline only; it trails P4+Q by 0.23. Stacking both beats P4+Q by about +0.35.

The bond-vs-equity divergence works only on the short side and only when measured inside the book. Dropping in-book names whose bond spread is tight relative to the equity-implied spread gives +0.26%/yr (t 2.58, raw p 0.010, Holm p 0.14, both halves positive). Buying names whose bond is wide relative to equity loses: -0.03 as an add-on and -0.06 standalone, with a sign flip across halves.

Early warning inside P4+Q: distance to default separates big losers well. Its AUC is 0.91 for 6-month losses below -10% (17 events) and 0.83 for losses below -5% (50 events). By comparison, carry scores 0.59, fundamentals quality 0.80 and 63-day equity return 0.83. The worst distance-to-default quintile caught 94% of the events held in P4+Q.

Issuer level: 50% of the 30 issuers with a first loss below -10% were in the worst distance-to-default quintile at decision time. Americanas (AMER3) was at the 0.9th percentile (distance to default 1.57) in November 2022, two months before the fraud disclosure. Casas Bahia (BHIA3), Oncoclinicas (ONCO3), KRSA3 and Simpar (SIMH3) were at the 2nd-3rd percentile.

Blind spot: only 52% of all losses below -10% have a distance to default, and 72% of those issuers are listed at all. The unlisted special-purpose-vehicle and water-utility tail cannot be seen through equity.

Lead-lag on weekly data, with week fixed effects and issuer-clustered errors: issuer equity returns lead bond spread changes by 1-4 weeks. Coefficients are -14.7, -12.5, -10.8 and -8.0 bps per 100% equity return at lags 0-3 (t -3.0 to -2.0), so a -10% equity week means about +4.6 bps of widening over the next month. The effect exists only for direct listings (-19, t -3.4) and not for parent listings (t 0.4). Bond spreads do not lead equity (t 0.5), and model distance-to-default changes add nothing (t -0.7). The effect is economically too small to trade after costs.
Sealed holdout, run once for the frozen best variant (Jan-Sep 2026): +0.39%/yr vs P4+Q (t 3.1 over 9 months), +3.7%/yr vs universe.
signals: research/nightly/structural_credit/signals.py: signals(panel) adds these columns to any harness panel: sc_dd (Merton distance to default), sc_dd_naive, sc_pd, sc_cg (CreditGrades bps), sc_lcg, sc_mlev, sc_dd_chg21, sc_dd_chg63, sc_lcg_chg63, sc_mcap, sc_sigE, sc_div (rank of cdi_bps minus rank of CreditGrades spread) and sc_div_res (residual of log cdi_bps on log CreditGrades spread and duration; positive means the bond is wide relative to equity).
Cached versions of the same columns: data/history/nightly/structural_credit/signals_M.pkl and signals_W.pkl, keyed by (codigo, cnpj8, day).

Recommended overlay: avoid the worst quintile of sc_cg or sc_dd inside P4+Q, e.g. p4q & ~(sc_cg >= per-date 80th percentile). Alternatively, the inside-book divergence avoid rule: the bottom 20% of sc_div_res among listed P4+Q names (run.py in_book_worst).
Underlying daily table with one row per (ticker, date): data/history/nightly/structural_credit/structural_daily.pkl, loaded via signals.load_daily().
caveats: No variant survives Holm correction across the 12 variants tried; the lowest adjusted p is 0.14. Marks are smooth and stale, which inflates the t-statistics.

Only 40% of P4+Q exposure has an equity-implied signal. The rules only ever remove listed names, so the book tilts toward unlisted, rarely-marked issuers, which is where survivorship bias lives. The placebo's +0.14 partly reflects this tilt.

The market-cap reconstruction is approximate. It anchors to today's brapi market cap and brapi's split adjustments, which are price-neutral but not strictly as-of. A few serial recapitalizers (SEQL3, AMER3 in 2024, AMBP3) remain noisy. Banks and insurers are excluded because they have no debt field.

For parent-listed issuers, the distance to default is the parent group's risk, not the issuer's. Gross debt excludes IFRS-16 leases, so the default point is understated for retailers with heavy lease obligations.

problems: No look-ahead or data-leakage defect was found. Every leakage probe left A3 at +0.33 to +0.35%/yr vs P4+Q, so leakage does not refute the result.

The gain depends on a few issuers. Forcing AMER3 back into the book cuts A3 to +0.26 (t 1.40), and the 2022-23 half goes to -0.01. Forcing ONCO3 back cuts it to +0.22 (t 1.17). Keeping the 3 worst dropped issuers (AMER3, ONCO3, AERI3) cuts it to +0.13 (t 0.89). In effect the rule mostly means 'avoided Americanas and Oncoclinicas'. This is a real equity-market signal (it was PIT, and AMER3's DD was already low in Nov 2022), but it amounts to only 2 or 3 independent events.

A3 was picked as the maximum of 12 variants. At t 1.65 (raw p about 0.10) with Holm p 0.998, the +0.35 point estimate carries winner's-curse upward bias. Their own model-free control C2 (52-week equity drawdown) gives +0.34 (t 1.84), so the structural model adds nothing.

The gain comes almost entirely from 2024. By year, A3 vs P4+Q is -0.04 in 2022, +0.38 in 2023, +1.33 in 2024 and -0.26 in 2025. Leaving out 2024 drops the full-period figure to +0.02 (t 0.09). The claim that 'both halves are positive' hides that 2 of the 4 years are flat or negative.
The gain is concentrated in a few months. Dropping the 3 best months (2024-12 +0.76%, 2023-01 +0.36%, 2024-04 +0.20%) leaves +0.02%/yr (t 0.18). Only 60% of months are positive.

The gain is concentrated in a few issuers. Excluding the top 1, 3, 5 and 10 contributing issuers from both books gives +0.24, +0.13, +0.07 and +0.01. The top 5 are ONCO3, AMER3, DASA3, AERI3 and CSNA3, all well-known 2023-24 blowups, so the result is about 4-5 tail avoidances, not a broad cross-sectional effect. That is plausible for a tail filter, but those names are exactly the ones a researcher would have in mind when designing it (a soft look-ahead in model or parameter choice).

wave1.headline: Text from CVM filings and news headlines, even with multilingual embeddings, zero-shot classes and full PDF text, does not beat P4+Q: the best overlay (drop names with a zero-shot credit-negative document in the last 90 days) adds +0.27%/yr before 2026 (t 1.28, Holm p=1), and filings do not lead spread moves; they follow them.
wave1.best: V4: P4+Q excluding issuers with any zero-shot credit-negative document (IPE or news, cosine > 0.55 to the rj/default/liab-mgmt/rating-down/guidance-cut/litigation/ofício prototypes) in (d-90, d-1]
insights: Disclosure lags the market. In the 60 days before the filing, liability-management filings see -1.2% abnormal bond return (t -2.7) and PDF-body hard events hidden behind clean titles see -5.1% (t -3.1, n=36). Returns after the filing are about 0 or positive.

Lead time is zero. Before 368 spread blow-outs (>=150 bps relative widening in 4 weeks), text flags appeared in the prior 13 weeks no more often than in random issuer-weeks: lift 0.91-1.04 for keyword, zero-shot, sentiment and Fato Relevante flags. 18-25% of blow-outs are flagged only during or after the widening.

The one post-event drift comes from event-risk corporate actions, not distress filings. M&A filings: -0.28% over 60 days (t -2.4), issuer spread +16 bps at 13 weeks (t 2.9). Guidance cut/impairment: -0.54% (t -2.2). CVM ofício: -0.24% (t -2.0). Placebo random dates: +0.16%. This is too small and rare to move a 100-name book.

Any news is bad news. The top-5% most POSITIVE sentiment docs underperform like the negative ones (-0.24% over 60 days, t -2.4). Generic filing counts have ICs as strong as the credit classes: ipe_one_90 IC -0.064, burst_30 -0.054, ipe_new_debt_180 -0.050, versus neg_kw_90 -0.044 and zs_neg_90 -0.047. The text signal is mostly issuer visibility or size, not meaning.
Liability-management filings mark the bottom: ipe_liab_mgmt_180 has a POSITIVE IC (+0.025, t 3.1 at 63 days), so it should not be used as an exclusion filter.
The most specific news signals are news_neg_kw_90 (IC -0.041, t -5.1), news_litigation_90 (-0.032, t -4.1) and news_rj_90 (-0.026, t -3.5). As overlays they still do not beat P4+Q after Holm.
A walk-forward ridge on 768-d mean embeddings (IPE + news, 90 days) has out-of-sample IC -0.006 (t -0.2). Supervised learning on text embeddings finds nothing.

Full text vs title (700 CVM PDFs, 98% extracted): 7.2% of filings with clean titles have hard credit-event language in the body, and 88% of hard titles are confirmed by the body. Title and body sentiment correlate 0.45. Reading bodies adds information, but the market has already priced it.

V4 is consistent across costs and scenarios: +0.24%/yr at 50 bps, +0.25 under rec40. The gain is concentrated in 2024-25 (+0.48 vs +0.06 in 2022-23). The names it removes still beat the universe (+0.46%/yr cohort). Sealed holdout 2026-01..09 (read once): +0.33%/yr vs P4+Q, t 1.53, 9 months. The sign is consistent but it is not significant.
signals: features.signals(panel) in research/nightly/text_nlp/features.py -> DataFrame[cnpj8, day, features] for any harness panel (M or W); join on (cnpj8, day). Cached for the monthly panel in data/history/nightly/text_nlp/text_signals_M.pkl.
zs_neg_90: count of zero-shot credit-negative docs in (d-90, d-1]. Best overlay: exclude from P4+Q when > 0.
neg_kw_90 / ipe_neg_kw_90 / news_neg_kw_90: keyword credit-negative counts. news_neg_kw_90 has IC -0.041 (t -5.1).
news_litigation_90 (IC -0.032, t -4.1) and news_rj_90 (IC -0.026, t -3.5).
ipe_liab_mgmt_180: positive IC (+0.025, t 3.1). A post-reprofiling recovery signal, not an exclusion.
ipe_mna_180 / ipe_guidance_cut_180 / ipe_oficio_90: event-risk flags with slow post-event drift.
ipe_one_90 / burst_30: filing-activity (visibility) proxies, IC -0.064 / -0.054.
sent_news_30 / sent_hot_30: embedding sentiment of news (weak).
txt_ml in data/history/nightly/text_nlp/txt_ml_M.pkl [cnpj8, day, codigo, txt_ml]: walk-forward ridge text score. IC about 0, not useful.
caveats: The news corpus comes from negative-keyword Google News queries: recall is relevance-capped, density rises strongly in 2025-26, and some headlines are off-topic.
IPE covers only CVM-registered issuers (384 of 775 grid issuers, about 83% of universe rows). Unlisted SPVs have no filings, so 'no text' does not mean 'clean'.
About 9 overlay variants, about 40 event classes and about 30 IC features were examined. Holm is applied across the overlays only, so treat event and IC t-stats below 3 as exploratory.
Marks are smooth and stale, which inflates Sharpe and t. Some event paths (RJ, n=11) are dominated by a few gap jumps, so medians are reported alongside means.

problems: There is no look-ahead or holdout leakage. V4 reproduces exactly: +0.267%/yr vs P4+Q, t 1.28. Adding 1, 3 or 7 extra days of availability lag to every document does not hurt it (+0.29, +0.30, +0.29), so the result does not depend on same-day information. The run only loads documents dated before 2026, and IPE availability uses Data_Entrega with the first delivery kept per protocol.

The value attributed to text meaning is mostly issuer filing activity. A content-shuffle placebo kept each embedded document's issuer and date but randomly permuted the zero-shot-negative flags (20 draws). It averages +0.18%/yr (p95 +0.30), and 15% of draws beat V4. Only about +0.09%/yr of V4 comes from what the documents say.

A control with no content at all beats V4. Excluding P4+Q issuers with any Fato Relevante, Comunicado, debenture notice or news item in the last 90 days gives +0.64%/yr (t 1.36; 43 names, all of it in 2024-25). Excluding issuers with any Fato Relevante gives +0.19%/yr. So the overlay works as a 'drop listed, visible, frequently-filing issuers' tilt, which confirms the README's own 'any news is bad news' insight.

The +0.27%/yr for V4 is concentrated in a few issuers. Leave-one-issuer-out shows one issuer (cnpj8 12104241) supplies +0.14 of the 0.27. Not excluding the top 3 contributing issuers leaves +0.009 (t 0.05); the top 5 gives -0.03 and the top 10 gives -0.08. The ranking is outcome-selected, so this test is harsh, but the V4 edge is not broad-based.

Removing the 5 best months turns it negative: without the top 3 months it is -0.06, without the top 5 it is -0.16. Only 52% of months are positive. By year: 2022 -0.28, 2023 +0.39, 2024 +1.03, 2025 -0.08, so the whole result is 2024, mainly Dec-2024 (+0.68% in one month). Without 2023 it is +0.23 (t 1.0).

Parameters were chosen on noise. By window at T=0.55: 30d +0.02, 60d +0.12, 90d +0.27, 180d +0.40. By threshold at 90d: T 0.50 +0.41, 0.55 +0.27, 0.60 +0.09, 0.65 +0.13. The gain grows with how many names are excluded, not with how precise the classification is.

wave1.headline: Filtering the marks (a Kalman filter per issuer, and volume-weighted clean prints) leaves the relative-value signal unchanged, so it is not a print-noise artifact; the real limit is execution: realistic costs by liquidity bucket cut P4+Q from +2.2 to about +1.2%/yr over CDI, and it falls to about +0.4 at R$500m and about 0 at R$2bn.
wave1.best: P4Q_gapfilter: P4+Q, skipping bonds whose last print is more than 2 sd rich versus the bond's own Kalman fair spread
insights: Relative value survives better marks, and the noise part predicts nothing. Spearman IC of resid_bps against fwd_126: 0.209 (t 11.5) on raw marks, 0.208 (t 15.1) on Kalman marks, 0.207 on volume-weighted marks. The noise component (raw minus Kalman resid) has IC 0.006 (t 0.3). RV is as strong in illiquid bonds (IC 0.19) as in liquid ones (0.21), and much stronger in DI (0.38) than in IPCA (0.16).

IPCA debenture prints come in two price tiers. Measured against the Kalman one-step prediction, tickets under R$200k print about 7-9 bps of price below fair (close to fair), while R$1-5m blocks print about 38 bps below and blocks over R$5m about 60 bps below (medians). DI floaters show under 1 bp. The typical IPCA print noise is about 75 bps of price, against about 4 bps for DI floaters.

The harness's 25 bps round trip is 2 to 5 times too low. Roll half-spreads on institutional-size prints are about 23 bps of price for DI and about 77 bps for IPCA/PRE. Round trips by ADV quintile are 45-65 bps for DI and 136-169 bps for IPCA. Taking all prints, the round trip is about 1.75 times higher.

Under liquidity-bucket costs with no size limit, P4+Q earns +1.16%/yr over CDI instead of +2.22, against +0.32 for the universe. With the all-prints Roll as an upper-bound cost, it earns +0.20 against -0.32.

Capacity, with fills capped at 20% of the bond's actual SND volume plus square-root impact: P4+Q earns +0.82%/yr over CDI at R$100m with 87% of the target filled, +0.41 at R$500m with 77% filled, and +0.04 at R$2bn with 59% filled. Its edge over the universe shrinks from +0.53 to +0.23 to +0.06. Total SND volume is about R$2.1-2.4bn per business day, and the median bond trades about R$0.9m a day.
P4+Q leans toward illiquid bonds: 27% of it sits in the least-liquid ADV quintile against 20% of the universe, and its median bond prints on 29% of days against 44%.

Liquidity-aware sizing (planned from past 63-day ADV, with the overflow going to the next-best carry names) adds +0.035, +0.10 (t 1.1) and +0.09%/yr at R$100m, R$500m and R$2bn. That is not significant.

Getmansky-Lo-Makarov de-smoothing (MA(2) on monthly excess): about 30-35% of monthly returns show up with a 1-2 month lag. Observed Sharpe falls from 2.13 to 1.57 for P4+Q, 1.81 to 1.31 for P4, 0.74 to 0.51 for the universe and 0.81 to 0.52 for the IDA-DI index. True volatility is about 1.4-1.5 times the observed. The P4+Q minus universe spread is much less smoothed (1.06 to 0.94).

Dropping the least-liquid quintile costs -0.14%/yr at 25 bps and is neutral under bucket costs. Ranking carry net of estimated cost helps only when costs are realistic (+0.21, t 0.8) and flips sign between the halves (+0.31 in 2022-23, -0.44 in 2024-25).
signals: research/nightly/marks_liquidity/signals.py: signals(panel) adds point-in-time columns to any harness panel.
kf_s / kf_sd: Kalman fair CDI+ spread and its uncertainty.
kf_gap / kf_gap_z: last print minus fair value; the P4Q_gapfilter variant drops kf_gap_z < -2.
kf_resid_bps / kf_resid_z: relative value against the peer curve, computed on Kalman marks.
vw_resid_bps / vw_resid_z: relative value computed on volume-weighted clean marks.
adv63, tdays63, ticket63, liq_q (ADV quintile within the universe), roll_hs.
cost_rt_bps: estimated round-trip cost (all-prints Roll by indexer group x ADV quintile; multiply by results.json costs.inst_scale for the institutional tier).
Raw cache: data/history/nightly/marks_liquidity/marks.pkl with (codigo, day, values).

run.py: tranche_book(T, aum=..., hs_b=..., sigma_b=..., adv_b=..., cumV=...), a harness-identical tranche engine with per-bond costs, square-root impact and volume-participation fills, for capacity tests.
caveats: SND only publishes daily aggregates per bond (average price, quantity, number of trades), with no intraday high/low or bid/ask. Corwin-Schultz therefore cannot be computed, and the Roll estimate mixes the retail/institutional price tiers with the true bid-ask spread. The institutional cost scale (0.57 for DI, 0.62 for IPCA) is a single pooled ratio.

The impact coefficient (1.0 x daily sigma x sqrt(trade / 63-day ADV)) is assumed, not estimated. Exits are assumed filled. Fills use the bond's actual volume in the entry window, as a simulation of what would have executed.
The IPCA CDI-equivalent spreads use a static duration factor and today's contract terms, so part of the large IPCA print noise may be a conversion artifact.
Kalman parameters are pooled by indexer group (issuer-common share fixed at 0.8 for DI, which is a cap, and 0.15 for IPCA) and estimated only on prints before 2024.

problems: The gap filter's edge is statistically and economically nil. It reproduces at +0.047%/yr vs P4+Q (t 1.09, Holm p 1.0) and +0.035 at 50 bps (t 0.81). It should not be read as adding value, and the agent does not claim significance.
The filter is fragile to its threshold. Cutoffs of -1.5, -2 and -2.5 give +0.06, +0.05 and +0.04, while -3 gives +0.02 (t 0.5).

The economic story does not hold. The mirror filter (skip bonds whose last print is >2 sd CHEAP vs fair) does better, at +0.096 (t 1.76), than the claimed rich-print filter. So what helps is removing noisy outlier prints in either direction, not specifically skipping rich prints.
The headline number reproduces exactly: P4Q_gapfilter beats P4+Q by +0.047%/yr (NW t 1.09, p 0.28, Holm p 1.0 across 7 variants). Statistically and economically this is zero, and the author says so.

The gain comes from 5 issuers. Excluding the top-5 contributing issuers (cnpj8 00776574, 12104241, 09527023, 44507288, 12528708) from both books turns the diff to -0.006 (t -0.2). Excluding the top 10 gives -0.030 (t -1.2).
It is not stable by year: 2022 +0.00, 2023 +0.08, 2024 +0.13, 2025 -0.03 (cumulative %). Excluding 2023 gives +0.036 (t 1.1).

wave1.headline: Buying new issues, upgraded names or redemption candidates does not pay, but dropping from P4+Q the issuers that just had an M&A filing, a downgrade, a debenture-holder meeting, a redemption notice or a recovery filing adds about +0.30%/yr (t 1.95, random-drop placebo 0 of 40, holdout +0.42). It does not survive Holm (p 0.51).
wave1.best: P4Q_exNegEvents: P4+Q minus issuers with an M&A/reorganisation filing or rating downgrade in the last 180d, a debenture-holder meeting (AGD) in the last 180d, an early-redemption notice in the last 126d, or a recovery (RJ) filing in the last 365d. All events are dated by CVM Data_Entrega and used strictly after that date.
insights: Credit-event drift is slow. Carry-adjusted, the issuer's universe bonds lose -1.54% over 126d after a rating downgrade (t -3.2, n=60) and -0.64% after an M&A, reorganisation or control-change filing (t -2.8, n=358). Most of the loss comes after day 21, so the edge is in staying out for months, not in trading fast.

Abstaining beats adding. All five exclusion overlays improve P4+Q (+0.03 to +0.17 on their own, +0.30 combined, halves +0.13 / +0.47). Every addition hurts: new issues -0.12, incentivised new issues -0.04, upgrades -0.02.

Placebo: dropping the same number of randomly chosen P4+Q issuers each date gives -0.02%/yr (p95 +0.10), and 0 of 40 draws beat the real +0.30. The gain comes from which names are dropped, not from concentrating the book.

Robustness of the exclusion overlay vs P4+Q: 50bps +0.27, rec40 +0.32 (t 2.0), hold63 +0.39, hold252 +0.28, cap5% +0.28, weekly tranches +0.32. On the sealed 2026 holdout (9 months) it was +0.42%/yr vs P4+Q (t 2.2), while P4+Q itself earned only +0.08 exCDI.

The new-issue premium is real but about the size of costs. Over the first weeks on the grid it is +0.24% carry-adjusted at 63d (t 2.9, n=1,486) and gone by 126d (+0.07). Only incentivised IPCA new issues keep +0.44% at 126d (t 3.7). Standalone new-issue sleeves lose to the universe (-0.21%/yr) and lost -4.2%/yr vs P4+Q in the 2026 holdout.

Buying redemption or call candidates does not pay on SND marks. After a redemption notice the bonds show -0.35% at 126d. Below-par bonds of issuers announcing redemptions show -1.15% (n=68), with no pull-to-par gain. Callable bonds above par show no negative-convexity penalty (+0.07, t 1.6).
A new bond from the same issuer (supply) does not cheapen its existing bonds: about 0 at every horizon, n=798. Equity raises are neutral for bondholders (+0.18 at 63d, -0.01 at 126d).

Seasoning: bonds more than 48 months after issue earn +0.45% carry-adjusted over 126d (t 6.0). These are low-carry bonds (~60 bps) near maturity, so this is likely pull-to-par or a misspecified carry control, not an event effect. It is flagged for the combiner, not traded.

The SND registry cannot date early exits, because 'Data de Vencimento' is overwritten with the exit date. None of the 130 registry-flagged 'RESGATE TOTAL ANTECIPADO' bonds since 2021 ever traded on SND, so redemption must be studied through the CVM IPE announcements.

problems: I found no look-ahead leak. The number reproduces exactly (+0.2996%/yr, t 1.95, halves +0.13/+0.47) from the cached signals, from signals rebuilt fresh, and from my own independent reimplementation. There are 0 mismatched cells between cached and fresh signals.

The event-timing mechanism does not hold up. I kept each issuer's own neg events and shifted all of them by one random offset per issuer (20 draws). That gives +0.22%/yr on average (p95 +0.33, max +0.41), and 3 of 20 draws reach the real +0.30. Only about +0.08%/yr can be attributed to the timing of events. The author's placebo drops random P4+Q issuers, so it does not control for the kind of issuer that files many CVM IPE documents, and it overstates the evidence (0 of 40).

Stale-event test, which is point-in-time: dropping issuers whose neg events are 365-730 days old, not recent, gives +0.33 (t 1.41). Dropping issuers that ever had a neg event before the decision date gives +0.54 (t 1.70). An issuer trait (frequent-filer, listed or complex groups) explains the gain as well as or better than the 126-365 day post-event drift the README claims.

The number reproduces exactly (vs P4+Q +0.2996%/yr, NW t 1.95, p 0.051; 50 bps +0.27, t 1.79), but the event-timing mechanism does not hold up. A placebo that keeps the same issuers and the same count of negative events per issuer, but assigns uniformly random dates, gives +0.43%/yr on average (p95 +0.52, max +0.59). The real rule, at +0.30, sits at the bottom of that distribution: 95% of the 20 draws are at least as good. Event timing adds nothing over issuer identity.

Point-in-time placebos match the real rule. Using only STALE events (every event shifted +365d, so the window covers events 1 to 1.5 years old) still gives +0.25 (t 1.47). Using 'neutral' events that should not predict losses (equity raise, new debenture offer, same-issuer supply, 180d) gives +0.40 (t 1.63). The overlay acts as a persistent 'active CVM filer / complex issuer' filter, not as a slow credit-event drift. The author's random-issuer-drop placebo (0/40) only shows that the dropped issuers differ from random P4+Q names, not that the events matter.

A few issuers drive it. Americanas (00776574) is by far the largest contributor. It was excluded before its January 2023 collapse because of AGD and M&A filings. Removing the top-5 contributing dropped issuers (Americanas, 38482780, Aeris, Oncoclinicas, Simpar) from BOTH books cuts the edge to +0.18%/yr (t 1.28, p 0.20), and the 2022-23 half turns negative (-0.06). Top-10 removed: +0.16 (t 1.17).

wave1.headline: An issuer-aware fair value is a 2.5x better spread model, and within-issuer cheap-vs-rich switches pay about +0.8%/yr per pair (t 6.4), but neither improves P4+Q: P4+Q already holds each issuer's cheap bonds, and the issuer part of resid_z is carry premium that pays. The best variant adds +0.03%/yr (t 0.65, Holm p=1), and the holdout gives -0.05.
wave1.best: tilt_carry+0.5eiss: P4+Q-style book (top 30% by score, not rich, no negative press, not worst quality quintile) ranked on cdi_bps + 0.5 x e_iss, where e_iss is the leave-one-out issuer-curve residual
insights: The peer residual resid_bps has two parts. The issuer component is persistent credit/carry premium: it pays and does not converge. The bond-within-issuer component is true relative value: its 13-week convergence beta is -0.37 (t -13.8, R2 12%), a half-life of about 20 weeks.

The issuer-aware fair value (e_iss, leave-one-out issuer mean) roughly doubles cross-sectional spread convergence: beta -0.23 vs -0.11, pooled R2 5.3% vs 2.1%. Its return IC is lower, though: fwd_126 IC 0.166 vs 0.209 for resid_bps. A better spread model is a worse return signal.
A sector-aware peer curve (r_sec) adds nothing over the kind x Lei 12.431 peer curve. Economic-group keys (e_grp) and an issuer slope correction (e_slope) are about equal to plain issuer keys.

Within-issuer switch, long the cheap and short the rich bond of the same issuer: +0.83%/yr at 126d (t 6.4, hit 59%, n=5,499) and +1.43%/yr at 63d (t 8.7). The random-pair placebo gives -0.01 (p95 +0.15). The halves are +0.74 (2022-23) and +1.01 (2024-25). The carry gap is 55 bps, so only about 0.3%/yr is convergence beyond carry.
Cross-indexer switches (DI+ vs IPCA+, compared in CDI+ equivalents) work as well as same-curve ones: +1.03%/yr, t 3.2.
Incentivada vs taxable within an issuer: the higher-spread, usually taxable, bond outperformed (+3.8%/yr, t 3.2), but on only 135 pairs. The residual sort fails there (-2.4).

Why books do not improve: the curve-residual switch changes only 4% of P4+Q slots (about 4 names a month), because P4+Q's carry ranking already picks each issuer's cheap bonds; the carry-switch control reproduces P4+Q exactly. The issuer-aware rich flag disagrees with resid_z on only about 5 top-carry bonds per date.
Pure RV books lose to P4+Q: top 20% by e_iss_z scores -0.98%/yr vs P4+Q (t -2.0), since stripping out the issuer carry premium removes the return.
Market-level basis timing does not work: IPCA-vs-DI basis t 1.0, incentivada basis t -1.2, over 44 months.

problems: The book-level claim is itself negative, and it reproduces exactly. tilt_carry+0.5eiss vs P4+Q gives +0.026%/yr (t 0.65), and +0.024 (t 0.59) at 50 bps. Against its own lambda=0 control it gives +0.032 (t 0.79). Permuting e_iss within each date gives -0.011 (t -0.23). Using e_iss one month stale gives +0.024 (t 0.94). No look-ahead or holdout leak was found in signals.py or run.py: the signals are same-day leave-one-out cross-sections, execution is at the harness's next trade, and the best variant was chosen on pre-2026 data only.

The tilt book is not exactly P4+Q at lambda=0. With lambda=0 it cuts on a cdi_bps quantile instead of cdi_pct, and that control trails P4+Q by -0.006%/yr (t -2.8). This is small and mechanical, but part of the reported difference is a change in how the book is defined, not the e_iss signal.

The within-issuer switch alpha is front-loaded, which looks like mark noise rather than 20-week convergence. On the same sample, ranking on a one-month-stale residual cuts the 126d switch return from +0.76 to +0.37%/yr (t 5.4 to 2.7). The 63d result is also larger per year than the 126d one. A 20-week half-life would keep about 85% after one month, so the 'true RV, half-life ~20w' reading, and the -0.37 within-issuer convergence beta, are likely inflated by mark noise and regression to the mean in the 13-week spread-change regression.

Nothing in the book level holds up. I reproduced tilt_carry+0.5eiss exactly: +0.026%/yr vs P4+Q, t 0.65, and +0.024 (t 0.59) at 50 bps. Dropping 2023 cuts it to +0.001 (t 0.01). Taking the top-5 contributing issuers out of the universe and re-running both books flips it to -0.038 (t -0.86). Those five issuers account for 165% of the attributed positive difference.

The λ grid is flat noise: 0.25 gives +0.027 (t 1.2), 0.5 gives +0.026, 0.75 gives +0.034, 1.0 gives +0.016, 1.5 gives -0.029 and 2.0 gives +0.005. The best variant was picked after the fact, and the λ=0 control (same quantile rule) sits at -0.006 vs P4+Q (t -2.8). About half of the 'gain' is just the quantile-vs-cdi_pct construction difference.

In a placebo where e_iss is shuffled within each date (20 draws), the null averages -0.016 with p95 +0.018, against the actual +0.026 (5% of draws at or above). That is marginal at best, and it disappears once you drop 2023 or the top-5 issuers. The tilt changes only about 4.75 of roughly 104 names per date.

wave1.headline: No network filter beats P4+Q: contagion from shocked neighbours (group mates, sibling bonds, sector, similar exposures, common fund holders) barely shows up inside P4+Q. The best filter adds +0.07%/yr (t 0.9, Holm p 1.0) and loses 0.06%/yr in the 2026 holdout. The one robust effect is sector 3-month momentum across the whole universe (t -4.3), which does not add value on top of P4+Q.
wave1.best: avoid_exposure_stress_q5: P4+Q minus the top-quintile names by exposure-similar neighbour stress (4-week return of issuers in other sectors with cosine similarity >= 0.5 on macro and commodity exposures)
insights: Group contagion is not there. Non-shocked bonds whose group mate had a hard shock earn -0.56%/yr over 63 days (t -0.5, n=4,041), and -1.17%/yr (t -0.7) when the mate's spread blew out. Brazilian corporate families are mostly ring-fenced concession special-purpose companies (Energisa 14 issuers, Motiva 15, Ecorodovias 14, Equatorial 14, EDP 10), and the market prices them as separate credits.

P4+Q already does the avoiding. The group-shock filters remove only 1-2 of about 100 P4+Q names per date, because the no-negative-press rule, rich exit and quality screen have already removed stressed networks. Most of the universe-level signals weaken or vanish inside P4+Q.

Sector 3-month momentum is the robust finding. Bonds in sectors whose other issuers fell over the last 13 weeks keep underperforming. The top-minus-bottom rank slope is -1.60%/yr at 63 days (Fama-MacBeth NW t -4.3), with t -3.0 in 2022-23 and -3.5 in 2024-25.

Sector momentum survives the obvious checks. Controlling for the bond's own 13-week return it is t -4.6. Skipping the first month (days 21 to 63) it is still -1.34%/yr (t -4.2). It fades by 126 days (t -1.3), so it is a 1-3 month lead-lag between sector mates, not own-bond momentum. Inside P4+Q it is only t -1.4 and as a filter it adds +0.00%/yr, including with 63-day tranches (+0.04, t 0.4).

The fund fire-sale channel points the wrong way. Bonds whose holding funds had the worst 21-day outflows did slightly better (+0.38%/yr at 63 days, t 0.9), and avoiding them costs -0.08%/yr (t -1.5). Holder exposure to spread shocks predicts nothing. Only the broad measure, holders exposed to any shock including press, is negative in the universe (t -2.4), and it disappears inside P4+Q.

Sibling-bond lead-lag appears only in 2024-25. When another bond of the same issuer falls 3% while this bond's mark is flat, the flat bond does -0.92%/yr over 63 days (t -2.1). The halves disagree: positive in 2022-23 and t -3.2 in 2024-25. As a filter it adds +0.01%/yr.

Stress among issuers with similar macro and commodity exposure in other sectors is the best lead inside P4+Q (Fama-MacBeth t -2.8). As a filter it gives +0.07%/yr vs P4+Q (t 0.92), +0.04 at 50 bps and +0.06 under the 40% recovery scenario. It beats randomly dropping the same number of names by about +0.10%/yr (random p95 +2.28 against +2.29), but it fails the sealed holdout at -0.06%/yr.
Randomly dropping about 22 names from P4+Q lowers returns (+2.19 on average vs +2.22). Any avoid filter should be judged against this drop-placebo, not against P4+Q itself.

caveats: Group, sector and exposure maps are static and carry today's structure back in time. Only the controller links from the CVM annual reference forms (FRE) and the fund holdings are dated.
Fund holdings for 2021-22 come from the CVM annual history files. They are used only from the reference date + 100 days, and confidential positions may be missing.
Marks are smooth and stale, so every t-stat is inflated. The sector-momentum lead-lag is partly a stale-mark effect and cannot be traded as a short, because debentures cannot be shorted.

12 variants were tried (10 in run.py plus 2 with 63-day tranches), and none survives Holm. The best variant was picked in-sample, so its +0.07 is biased upward, and it is -0.06 vs P4+Q in the sealed holdout (Jan-Sep 2026, run once).

problems: The best filter's +0.07%/yr over P4+Q is not a directional signal. Flipping the sign (dropping the LEAST exposure-stressed quintile) gives +0.076%/yr (t 0.8), slightly more than the claimed filter. The 'best' variant is a drop-any-quintile artefact, not contagion avoidance.
It is fragile. Using features one panel date staler (>= 1 week lag) gives -0.02%/yr (t -0.3). Quintile cutoffs 0.7 and 0.9 give +0.03%/yr each. It survives only at the exact cutoff that was picked.

Exposure-similarity is built from static sector-level exposure vectors, so the feature has only ~23 distinct values per date inside P4+Q. It works as a coarse sector filter, and today's exposure and sector maps are carried back in time (static-map look-ahead, which the README discloses).

The multiple-testing count of 12 is understated. The portfolio filters were chosen after running a Fama-MacBeth screen on 13 features x (fwd_21, fwd_63, within-P4+Q) and a 7-event study, and some untried nearby specifications do just as well (exp_any q0.8 gives +0.09, t 1.26). The negative conclusion is unaffected.

Insight 6 does not match the filter it describes. It cites the within-P4+Q Fama-MacBeth t of -2.8, but that t belongs to exp_any (share of exposure-similar issuers shocked). The filter actually used, avoid_exposure_stress_q5, is built on exp_r4, whose within-P4+Q Fama-MacBeth t is only -0.9.

The drop-placebo is a weak null. Randomly dropping the same number of names from P4+Q lowers the return (60 draws average +2.16 against +2.22 for P4+Q), so beating random drops (1.7% of draws at or above the variant; the original 20 draws gave 5%) mostly reflects the cost of dropping names. It is not evidence of a signal. The right comparison is the paired test against P4+Q, which is insignificant.

wave1.headline: Almost all of the value from portfolio construction comes from concentrating on the highest-carry P4+Q names (top-25 by carry: +1.76%/yr over P4+Q, t 4.7, Holm p<0.001), and risk models add nothing. But that premium sits in illiquid bonds: once positions are capped at liquidity, the edge drops to about +0.2 to +0.6%/yr at R$500m and disappears by R$1bn.
wave1.best: top25_carry_cap5: equal weight over the 25 highest-carry P4+Q names, issuer cap 5%, monthly 126-day tranches. It is statistically equivalent to mv_emp_g20 / mv_emp_g20_durband. It is NOT feasible for a R$500m fund. The recommended fund book is mv_emp_g20_fund500m: +0.57%/yr vs P4+Q, t 2.5, Holm p 0.30, so not significant after correction.
insights: Within P4+Q, carry still strongly predicts 6-month returns (Spearman IC +0.33, t 11). Equal weight throws that away. Top-25-by-carry scores +1.76%/yr vs P4+Q: +1.42 in 2022-23, +2.11 in 2024-25, +1.73 at 50 bps, +1.68 in rec40.

A mean-variance optimizer with de-smoothed empirical covariance (+1.62, t 4.1) ends up holding essentially the same book as top-25-by-carry. Measured correlations are close to zero, so the optimizer reduces to 'max carry subject to caps'. The risk model adds nothing.

Stale marks crush measured correlations: same-issuer bond pairs average only 0.18, sector 0.12 and market 0.09, even on 4-week sums. That is why empirical covariance models need structural floors (DTS model floors: issuer 0.8, sector 0.35, market 0.2) plus a default copula to see concentration risk.

Every risk-based construction loses to equal weight: min-var -0.33, inverse-vol DTS -0.43, max-diversification -0.41, issuer risk parity -0.20, CVaR with default scenarios -0.19 / -0.33 %/yr vs P4+Q. They underweight high-DTS carry and only modestly cut drawdown (min-var -0.84 vs P4+Q -1.39).

Duration x spread (DTS) predicts rate-hedged returns negatively (IC -0.23, t -3.2) while carry predicts them positively. The efficient tilt is high spread at short or neutral duration: the MV book held within a duration band was the best in-sample (+1.84, t 4.7).

The ex-ante tail model and realised history disagree. The default-scenario model (PD from spreads, 40% recovery, Gaussian copula) gives the concentrated books a 6-month CVaR99 of 9.7% vs 6.1% for P4+Q, yet realised max drawdown was smaller (-0.15 to -0.34 vs -1.39). In-sample default losses were far below even half of the risk-neutral PDs, so the premium is partly short default-cluster risk.

Capacity curve for the top-25-carry book with each position capped at 25% of the bond's 91-day SND volume, vs P4+Q: R$50m +0.99, R$100m +0.83, R$250m +0.46, R$500m +0.21, R$1bn -0.09, R$2bn -0.18 %/yr. At R$500m the unconstrained MV book would need a median of 174 days to build a position at 20% participation, and 50% of its weight breaches the liquidity cap.

The engine choice is purely a cost question. Replacing the book costs weekly -1.42 (14.5x/yr turnover, 1.8%/yr cost) and monthly -0.30 vs P4+Q. Bands and a 45% hysteresis buffer barely help (-0.02 / +0.02). Quarterly replace (+0.29) and 252-day tranches (+0.15) are the cheapest ways to hold P4+Q.
Issuer cap 5% vs 10% and a 25% sector cap cost nothing (+0.01). Full fund constraints on an equal-weight book (liquidity, duration band, min lot) cost -0.10 at R$500m and -0.23 at R$2bn.

Sealed holdout, 2026-01 to 2026-09, run once after freezing the recommendation. The universe returned -3.26%/yr and P4+Q +0.08. The recommended mv_emp_g20_fund500m returned +0.68 (+0.60 vs P4+Q, t 1.5). The unconstrained top-25-carry book returned +2.65 (+2.57 vs P4+Q, t 3.4). The fund-constrained equal-weight book was -0.16 vs P4+Q. CVaR lambda 5 was -0.53 vs P4+Q.
Placebo for the recommended book: the same weights on random universe names return +0.81 on average (p95 +1.04), against +2.79 actual.

caveats: Marks are smooth, stale and survivorship-biased, so the t-stats are inflated. The concentrated high-carry books load on exactly the illiquid, less-covered, less-listed names where this bias lives: the MV book is 46% covered vs 65%, and only 86% of its weight executes vs 92%.

Only 48 pre-2026 months, with few defaults among the chosen names. The default-scenario model says the concentrated books carry about 1.6x the tail (CVaR99 9.7% vs 6.1%). rec40 only stresses the 55 known stop-trading names.

34 variants are in the Holm correction. Several were added after seeing the first results (mv_emp_g20_durband, top25_carry_*, mv_emp_g20_fund500m, carry_over_var_tilt). Only the unconstrained carry-concentration books survive Holm. The recommended fund book does not (Holm p 0.30).

The liquidity proxy is SND reported R$ volume, which includes back-to-back trades, and the 25%-of-91-day-volume participation cap is an assumption. Real capacity is likely lower. There is no market impact beyond cost_bps, so impact would hurt the concentrated books most.

problems: LEAKAGE (harness-wide, not specific to this agent): cdi_bps and the par accrual in the daily returns both use TODAY's SND contract spread for the whole history (rfmonitor/ml/selection.py reference() -> mkt_rate; run_selection_lab.build_returns gpar). SND pct_curve is relative to the PU-par in force at each trade date, so the spread that actually accrued can be backed out from pu_avg/pct_curve. That comparison shows 270 DI_SPREAD bonds whose accruing spread changed by more than 0.5pp over the sample (repactuations: TEND14/15, ANIM12, OUSA11, FAZE11, KRSA21, JSMLA, VLME, AERI, and others). The top-25 book is overweight these names: 15.5% of its weight has a positive look-ahead gap, versus 11.9% of P4+Q, with a weighted gap of +0.10pp versus +0.04pp. So the carry ranking and the returns are both slightly inflated. After correcting the returns and re-ranking on point-in-time implied carry, the edge is +1.61%/yr (t 4.35), against the claimed +1.76. Halves are +1.30 / +1.93, and the 50 bps edge is +1.58.

SURVIVORSHIP stress (rec40 only covers the 55 bonds whose last mark was below 0.90). If every bond that stopped trading early with a last mark below 0.98 (150 bonds) is instead marked to 40% recovery, the corrected edge falls to +1.12%/yr (t 1.5, not significant). 2024-25 falls to +0.61. The concentrated high-carry book is more exposed to this bias than P4+Q, as the README says in its caveats. This is a stress case, not the truth: many early stops are redemptions at par.

CONCENTRATION: 3 issuers (cnpj8 12647827, 09074183, 12979552) supply about 35% of the edge over P4+Q. Removing them from both books ex post leaves +1.06 (t 2.6); removing the top 10 leaves +0.74 (t 2.0). The edge is robust in sign but smaller than the headline implies.

Reproduced exactly: an independent reimplementation and their own topk_carry() both give +1.761%/yr vs P4+Q (NW t 4.74). The headline number is real in this harness, but it is not new. It is the HY-lab result already published in research/out/HY_README.md: HY D10 plus the P4 filters and quality screen beat P4 by +1.6 (t 4.6). The README does not cite it.

The edge disappears in the segment where marks can be trusted. Restricted to issuers with fundamentals coverage, top-25 carry vs P4+Q is -0.02%/yr (t -0.05). Against a covered-only P4+Q it is +0.52 (t 1.36, n.s.). Listed issuers only: -0.32 vs P4+Q, and +0.28 (t 1.0) vs a listed-only P4+Q. The whole premium sits in uncovered and unlisted issuers: top-25 holds 45% covered names vs 65% for P4+Q. That is exactly where the harness README says survivorship and stale-mark bias live. rec40 only stresses 55 bonds, so it cannot clear this.

The edge is concentrated in a few issuers. On cohort labels, the top 5 issuers supply 43% of the excess contribution. Removing them from the candidate set cuts the edge to +0.86 (t 1.99, p 0.046) vs P4+Q, or +1.07 (t 2.6) vs a P4+Q that also drops them. Removing the top 10 gives +0.77 (t 2.1).

wave1.headline: None of the 28 hedges or overlays beats P4+Q net of costs; the harness's 1:1 IPCA+ rate hedge over-hedges (debenture yields move only ~0.45x NTN-B), which inflates the IPCA+ sleeve's 2024-25 excess; the best realistic tool is skipping new tranches after a 63-day Ibovespa slump, which cuts maxDD from -1.39% to -1.10% for about -0.10%/yr.
wave1.best: E_gate_ibov: on a monthly decision date, skip the new P4+Q tranche (it stays in cash) when the Ibovespa's 63-day excess over CDI is below -10%. 4 of 48 decisions were gated: 2022-07, 2023-01, 2024-12 and 2025-01.
insights: The harness's IPCA+ rate hedge over-hedges. Point-in-time trade-to-trade regressions give a yield beta of IPCA+ debentures to NTN-B of 0.37-0.55 (0.52 in 2021, about 0.40 in 2023-24). As a result, the hedged IPCA+ P4+Q sub-book has a +1.23% per +1pp beta to the 5y real yield; with no hedge it is -2.37.

At the point-in-time empirical hedge ratio, the IPCA+ sub-book's excess over CDI falls from +1.87 to -0.20%/yr, and in 2024-25 from +4.47 to +0.33. The whole P4+Q book falls from +2.22 to +1.76 (-0.45%/yr, t -1.8). Monthly regressions put the zero-beta ratio at about 0.65, so the artifact is 0.3-0.45%/yr of the book. Any nightly result that favours IPCA+ bonds or looks strong in 2024-25 is suspect.

The IPCA+ sleeve's drawdown comes from inflation carry vs CDI, not from duration. Adding an IPCA x DI carry swap to the exact hedge cuts the sub-book maxDD from -5.05% to -2.17% (vol 2.71 to 2.25) and improves its excess from +1.87 to +2.63. At book level this is +0.14%/yr (t 0.9), for about 0.10%/yr of DAP/swap cost (book DV01 about 1.3 years).

Hedging IPCA+ bonds with nominal DI1 instead of DAP/NTN-B is disastrous: sub-book vol goes from 2.7% to 6.9% and maxDD from -5% to -14%. A single-vertex duration hedge costs little against bond-by-bond key-rate hedging (book maxDD -1.56 vs -1.39). Our B3/Tesouro key-rate curve reproduces bench_rate (correlation 0.999).

The book has essentially no linear equity, bank or sovereign beta: rolling Dimson betas average 0.003 (Ibov), 0.002 (SMAL11), 0.001 (banks) and 0.011 (EMBI CDS proxy), so beta hedges change results by -0.02 to -0.04%/yr. But in the book's 6 worst months the correlation with Ibov and banks is +0.72 to +0.76: stress is shared but asymmetric, so a conditional gate helps slightly and a linear hedge does not.

1m 10%-OTM Ibovespa puts cost about 0.11% of notional per month and paid off in 2 of 48 months. At 25% notional they cost 0.10%/yr and worsen maxDD (-1.63). The 2023 debenture stress was idiosyncratic.

Book-level overlays executed at the mark lose to switching costs and whipsaw. A drawdown stop switched 76 times, lost 1.1%/yr and worsened maxDD to -3.7%. Vol targeting cut vol from 1.04 to 0.78 but Sharpe fell from 2.13 to 1.81 (-0.81%/yr, Holm-significant negative). Universe-momentum lost 1.78%/yr. A 10% cash buffer is just proportional scaling (-0.22%/yr).

E_gate_ibov lost -0.10%/yr (t -0.9; -0.08 at 50 bps) for maxDD -1.10 vs -1.39 and worst month -0.53 vs -0.62. Only 7.5% of 40 random 4-gate placebos match that maxDD. In the sealed holdout (2026-01..09, evaluated once) it beat P4+Q by +0.12 (t 0.75), with maxDD -0.62 vs -0.78.

Bond-level stops: selling after a -3% 4-week drop gives vol 0.80 and maxDD -0.95 but costs 0.25%/yr, all of it in 2024-25. Selling below 95% of par costs 0.44%/yr. The weekly 'sell when rich' exit is the only exit that adds anything (+0.06, t 0.8).

Long-short within peers (theoretical; we found no organised debenture borrow market on B3): long P4+Q vs short the lowest-carry 30% of the same peers gives about 0 excess (-0.01%/yr at 2% borrow, -2.9% at 5%), with -0.58 correlation to the universe. The carry premium is on the long side only.
