caveats: Smooth, stale SND marks inflate Sharpe and t-stats and understate drawdowns. Book-level overlays are executed at the mark for the whole book, which is optimistic because debentures cannot be sold that way.
48 months with one idiosyncratic credit stress (2023) and no market-wide crash. Tail hedges are designed for a 2020-type event, which is absent from the sample.
The EMBI+ Brazil series (Ipeadata) ends 2024-07-30, so the CDS proxy has no hedge after that and ignores the USD quanto effect. Put pricing is Black-Scholes with IV = max(realised 63d, 15%) x 1.25.
The carry swap uses a daily-reset fixed leg at the NTN-B real yield; a real IPCA x DI swap locks the coupon at inception.

problems: No look-ahead in E_gate_ibov. Decisions are made at the close of day d and use Ibovespa closes up to d; execution starts at d+1. Ibov dates are correctly aligned (for example, the 2022-06-16 holiday is absent), and all decision dates are on the grid. The result reproduces exactly: -0.10%/yr (t -0.87), maxDD -1.099, and -0.08 at 50 bps.

The drawdown benefit rests on one gate, the 2023-01-02 decision. Gating only that decision gives maxDD -1.14 and +0.05%/yr. Leaving it out gives maxDD -1.37 (about the same as P4+Q's -1.39) and -0.16%/yr. That day's signal is -12.0%, set by the Ibovespa close on the decision day itself (inauguration-day drop). The rest of P4+Q's peak-to-trough (Dec-22 to Apr-23, Americanas/Light) is idiosyncratic.

Knife-edge timing. Adding one extra day of lag drops the 2023-01 gate and gates 2023-05 instead. The result becomes -0.22%/yr (t -2.69) with maxDD -1.37, so the drawdown gain disappears. A 5-day lag gives -0.32%/yr (t -2.62) and maxDD -1.35.

The numbers reproduce exactly with an independent reimplementation of E_gate_ibov (pre-2026, harness v4): diff vs P4+Q is -0.10%/yr (t -0.87) at 25 bps and -0.08 at 50 bps, maxDD is -1.099 vs -1.393, and the same 4 decisions are gated (2022-07, 2023-01, 2024-12, 2025-01). The headline that nothing beats P4+Q net of costs is CONFIRMED.

The maxDD benefit of the 'best realistic tool' comes from a single decision. Gating only 2023-01 gives maxDD -1.137 and +0.05%/yr. Gating only 2022-07, 2024-12 or 2025-01 gives maxDD -1.37 to -1.39, i.e. no drawdown gain, and costs -0.03 to -0.09%/yr each. So in effect this is one lucky skip of the tranche opened just before Americanas. That followed the post-election Ibov slump, which was a political equity move, not a credit signal.

The gate is not robust to small parameter changes. At a -12.5% or -15% threshold only 2022-07 is gated and maxDD is -1.367, so the gain is gone. At -7.5% the cost is -0.34%/yr (t -2.0). With an 84d window the cost is -0.37 (t -3.5) with maxDD -1.31; with a 126d window it is -0.58 (t -3.5) with maxDD -1.37; with a 21d window there is no DD gain. If the signal is 5 business days stale, the cost is -0.32%/yr (t -2.6) and maxDD is -1.35. Only the 42d window (maxDD -1.07, -0.04%/yr) reproduces the effect, and it also depends on gating 2023-01.

wave1.headline: Adding NTN-B, listed CRI funds, FIDC or CDI sleeves to P4+Q did not beat P4+Q: the best mix (80% P4+Q, 20% FIDC senior P4Q) adds only +0.14%/yr (t 0.7, Holm p 1.0). The FIDC returns it relies on are self-reported and not investable. In the one market-priced CRI vehicle (listed FII de papel), the P4 carry rule loses 4%/yr against that sleeve's own universe, and loses more in 2026.
wave1.best: MIX_80deb_20fidc (80% P4+Q debenture tranche book + 20% FIDC senior quotas picked P4Q-style: top 30% by trailing 3-report excess return, minus worst-quintile delinquency)
insights: P4 carry logic transfers only where marks are smooth and self-reported. FIDC senior P4Q beats the FIDC universe by +4.1%/yr (t 4.9, positive in both halves, above the placebo p95 of -0.3%, and +3.0%/yr in the 2026 holdout). The same rule on listed CRI funds priced on B3 (FII de papel) loses -4.0%/yr against the FII universe (t -1.9), sits below its random-book placebo (p = 0.77), and loses -12.2%/yr in the 2026 holdout. The losers are CACR11 (-60%), HCTR11 (-36%) and DEVA11 (-32%). High trailing yield there signals distress, not carry. This suggests part of the debenture/FIDC P4 edge is a mark-smoothing artefact.
FII price-to-NAV is not a value signal. Cheap-to-NAV CRI funds returned -9.7%/yr excess over CDI against -5.2 for the FII universe: discounts come before NAV write-downs.

NTN-B has about zero monthly correlation with P4+Q (0.01) but cost 2.6%/yr against CDI over 2022-25 (IMA-B5 after a 0.20% ETF fee; IMA-B -4.3, IDKA-2A -2.7). An 80/20 P4+Q/IMA-B5 mix is -0.97%/yr vs P4+Q (t -4.1). A 126-day trend filter on the NTN-B leg recovers +0.38%/yr, but the mix is still -0.59 (t -4.0).
After Geltner de-smoothing, P4+Q's Sharpe is still 1.55 (AR1 0.31), well above any market-priced sleeve. Inverse-vol or risk-parity mixing of P4+Q, IMA-B5 and FII only dilutes it (-2.76%/yr vs P4+Q).

Using CRI/CRA arrears (CVM securitisation reports) as an exclusion filter on debentures does nothing. 303 debtor/cedent issuers were ever flagged, but on average only 0.21 bonds in the debenture universe and 0.02 in P4+Q belong to them, so the two credit universes barely overlap.

Data feasibility. Free point-in-time market prices do not exist for CRI/CRA (ANBIMA public files 404, the Feed API is not approved, B3 has no free trade file), LF/CDB (CVM CDA holdings give accrual only; R$621bn of LF held by funds, median LF DI+ spread 0.99%) or eurobonds (FRED keeps ICE BofA EM/LatAm corporate indices only from 2023-09-29). Fiagro history on brapi is under 1 year, and FI-Infra distributions on brapi are incomplete. CVM securitisation reports cover 4,628 CRI/CRA certificates with a 58-day filing lag, but their values are book values (20% unchanged month on month).

FIDC senior sleeve: research/nightly/universe_expansion/run.py fidc_series(rule in {'U','P4','P4Q','Qonly'}, holdout=False, missing='cdi'|'zero') returns a daily excess series on the harness grid.

FII-CRI sleeve: run.py fii_targets(rule) + sleeve_book(fii_matrix(), targets); features in data/history/nightly/universe_expansion/fii_panel.pkl as (ticker, day, dy12, pnav, nav_chg6, nav_chg12, mom126, vol63, adtv).
Rates sleeves: run.py index_sleeves() returns the NTN-B, pre and LFT index excess over CDI (after ETF fee) on the grid; raw series in data/history/nightly/universe_expansion/index_sleeves.pkl.
Pre-2026 daily series of all sleeves and mixes: data/history/nightly/universe_expansion/series_pre2026.pkl ({'S': sleeves, 'A': allocations}).
caveats: FIDC returns are self-reported and smooth. About 84% of FIDCs are closed-end, and senior quotas are mostly untradeable, so the best mix is a paper result.

Open FIDC data has no delivery date, so availability was assumed at reference month-end + 45 days. Treating a missing monthly report as earning CDI is optimistic: if it earns 0% instead, FIDC P4Q is -0.9%/yr vs P4+Q.

FII-CRI universe = tickers brapi still resolves today, so it is survivorship-biased upward (and still negative). Distribution units and splits were repaired heuristically. Returns are pre-tax, although FII distributions are tax-exempt for individuals.
Index sleeves are ETF proxies: a 0.20%/yr fee is deducted, but tracking error and bid/ask are ignored. Mixes use fixed daily weights as an approximation to monthly rebalancing.

problems: The code does not use the availability lag the README states. build.py and run.py say a FIDC report is available at ref month-end + 45 days, but fidc_series uses ref <= m-2 at the start of month m. That is only about 31 days after month-end: the November report is used on 1 January but, under their own rule, would only be available on 14 January. With a lag of m-3, which matches the stated 45 days, the best mix's diff vs P4+Q goes from +0.14 to -0.11%/yr (t -0.46; 2024-25 half -0.32). FIDC P4Q ex-CDI falls from 2.95 to 1.67, and FIDC P4Q vs the FIDC universe from +4.06 to +3.17.

The FIDC sleeve pays no transaction costs, while the debenture book it is compared with pays 25 or 50 bps. The claimed '+0.22 at 50 bps' therefore improves only because P4+Q gets more expensive. Charging 25 bps on sum|dw| of the FIDC book gives a mix diff of -0.01. With both the m-3 lag and 25 bps it is -0.27 (t -1.03).

Implausible 'senior' returns, most likely data errors, drive the within-FIDC carry result. Selected classes include trailing excess over CDI of up to 14.5%/month. On average 4.6 selected classes a month have more than 2%/month excess. Examples: 29.492.605 Senior 1 reports 4-5%/month; 45.207.484 Senior 1 reports 5-7%/month with -103% unit-error rows. An ex-ante plausibility screen that drops classes with any trailing |excess| >= 2%/month cuts 'FIDC P4Q vs FIDC universe' from +4.06 to +2.23%/yr. With a 1%/month screen it is +1.56. So the '+4.1%/yr, t 4.9' insight is overstated by roughly half.

The FIDC sleeve (fidc_series in run.py) charges no transaction costs, even though the P4Q-style picks turn over every month, and mix() adds nothing because its weights are constant. Charging 25 bps on the FIDC turnover moves the best mix from +0.144 to -0.011%/yr vs P4+Q (t -0.05).

The reported '+0.22 vs P4+Q at 50 bps (t 1.06)' is an artefact of that. Only the debenture leg paid 50 bps; the FIDC leg stayed free. With 50 bps on both legs the mix is -0.09%/yr vs P4+Q at 50 bps (t -0.40).

The availability rule is not enforced as documented. The README says FIDC data is available at ref month-end + 45 days, and the panel's own 'avail' column is about ref + 75 days. The code uses ref <= m-2 months, i.e. a report is used about 15 days before its stated availability date. Enforcing it (lag 3 months) gives -0.11%/yr vs P4+Q (t -0.46), and the second half 2024-25 turns to -0.32. The real CVM filing deadline (about 15 days) is probably shorter, so this is a documentation inconsistency more than true look-ahead.

wave1.headline: Under conservative assumptions P4+Q falls from +2.22 to about +1.20%/yr over CDI, but its edge over the universe mostly survives: +1.12 becomes +0.95%/yr (t 2.05), with the same assumptions applied to both books.
wave1.best: honest_P4Q: holiday-accrual fix, 40% recovery for bonds of distressed issuers that went silent, execution at raw prints, exits only at real trades, liquidity-bucket costs, fundamentals lagged 90 days. It is a bias-adjusted baseline, not a strategy.
insights: New bug in run_selection_lab.build_returns (patched returns used by the harness). Carry accrues over np.busday_count, which counts weekdays, but the SND par curve accrues over B3 business days. Each weekday holiday therefore adds about 0.9 bp (DI), 2.7 bp (IPCA) or 5.4 bp (PRE) of fake return. That is 48 holidays and 54,610 rows. It inflates every book level by about 0.13%/yr and cancels in P4+Q−U.

Costs drive the level haircut. Liquidity-bucket institutional round trips (DI 45-65 bps, IPCA 136-169 bps) cut P4+Q by 0.81 and U by 0.64. P4+Q−U falls only 0.18, from 1.12 to 0.94. An independent ANBIMA bid/ask cross-section (10k quotes, DI 64-77 bps, IPCA 82-185 bps) gives nearly the same answer: P4+Q 1.37, P4+Q−U 0.85.

The Q filter is the fragile part. A 90-day lag on fundamentals cuts P4+Q−P4 from 0.33 to 0.26 alone, and to 0.20 (t 1.4) in the honest stack. Removing brapi rows or using non-strict dates changes nothing, so staleness hurts and restatement leakage does not.

No meaningful parameter snooping. P4 sits at the 54th percentile and P4+Q at the 57th of 72 neighbouring rules (carry cut, rich threshold, press filter, worst-Q quantile). The median neighbour P4+Q−U is 1.05 against 1.12 for the chosen rule, and the 10th percentile is 0.78.

Engine timing optimism is small or reversed. Forcing exits at real trades raises P4+Q by 0.05. Executing at raw rather than spike-cleaned prints is neutral. Entry latency of +1 day costs nothing and +5 days costs 0.08. The edge does not rely on same-day information.

Survivorship is small for P4+Q. P4+Q held 12 of 33 PIT distress issuers at their event (Dasa, Giga+, Oncoclinicas, Aeris, Ambipar, Americanas). Most kept trading, so the losses are already in the marks: Oncoclinicas bonds -28% around the event. The real hole is bonds that print near par and then go silent (Americanas LAMEA4/5). A 40% recovery on those costs only 0.07. The harsh variant, every stop below 0.98 set to 40%, costs 0.38 on the level and 0.23 on P4+Q−U.

7.3% of SND volume (527 codes) never reaches the grid. 226 of these codes have no % PU da Curva: %CDI, IGP-M or TR bonds, including Americanas LAME29/LAMEA1-3, CVC, Oi and Azul11. Off-grid bonds crash below 70% of par more often (6.6% vs 4.1%). This mildly flatters U but cannot flatter P4.

The P4+Q−U spread is barely smoothed (GLM theta0 0.92, Sharpe 0.96 observed vs 0.92 de-smoothed). Honest P4+Q's own Sharpe falls from 1.23 to 0.87 once de-smoothed. Random books with the same churn lose 1.23%/yr to honest U, because U's tranche book turns over about 1.7x/yr against about 3x for P4+Q.

Buy-at-PU-max / sell-at-PU-min is not a valid cost model for IPCA bonds. The SND intraday range grows with liquidity (median round trip 525 bps in the top IPCA quintile) because retail and institutional prints mix, while DI floaters show about 1 bp. It punishes the IPCA-heavy universe and artificially inflates P4+Q−U.
Sealed holdout (2026-01 to 2026-09, reported once): honest P4+Q -1.44%/yr vs honest U -3.96%/yr, so P4+Q−U is +2.52 (t 2.8). The relative edge held and the level did not. It is 9 months only.

caveats: The ANBIMA bid/ask comes from a single Sep-2026 cross-section (historical files return 404) and is applied back to 2022 by liquidity bucket. Liquidity quintiles use lifetime ADV (mild look-ahead, acceptable for a cost haircut but not for a signal).

The distress recovery rule is a judgement call and some of the 25 bonds hit were probably redeemed at par, which makes it conservative. A first, over-inclusive list (cdi_bps>1000, i.e. IPCA-conversion noise flagging 83 issuers and 199 bonds) was rejected and documented.

Not fixed: static contract terms (repactuations), the static duration factor in cdi_bps and the hedge, IPCA 'hedged' returns that keep NTN-B-vs-CDI carry, and the IDA overlay (not audited). Capacity is excluded (see marks_liquidity).

The honest P4+Q vs v4 P4+Q comparison (-1.02, t -7.6) is a mechanical haircut, not a strategy test. 162 backtests were run including the 72-rule neighbourhood, and Holm was applied across the 21 compared rows.

problems: It does not claim to add value over P4+Q, and it does not. diff_vs_p4q = -1.018 (t -7.6) is a haircut: the same book under harsher assumptions, not a new strategy. Holm p ≈ 0 is trivially true here because costs are deterministic and add up.

The empirical holiday check in results.json points the wrong way. With clipping, DI rows that cross a holiday average 0.37 bp, while rows that don't cross average 1.26 bp. That is noisy return data, not evidence for the bug. The bug itself is real: a direct test of the par curve (below) confirms it.

Liquidity quintiles use lifetime ADV, which is look-ahead (the audit discloses this). It is immaterial. With flat per-group costs, P4Q-U is 0.959. With quintiles from each bond's first 126 business days of ADV, it is 0.944. With lifetime ADV, it is 0.953.

Nothing here adds value over P4+Q, and the audit never claimed it did. Its diff_vs_p4q of -1.018 is a haircut: the honest stack against v4 P4+Q. It reproduces exactly: -1.0178, NW t -7.59, h1 -1.20, h2 -0.83, and every year from 2022 to 2025 is negative.

The claim that the edge over the universe 'mostly survives (+0.95, t 2.05)' is fragile under the robustness lens. Excluding 2023: +0.90, t 1.61. Excluding the top-5 contributing issuers from both books: +0.74, t 1.54 (P4+Q only: +0.67, t 1.46). Institutional bucket costs x1.5: +0.78, t 1.67. Only the three most liquid ADV quintiles tradable (capacity proxy): +0.73, t 1.71. By year: 2022 +1.82, 2023 +1.12, 2024 -0.06, 2025 +0.93. Only the base case clears t = 2.

The relative edge exists only because the universe benchmark pays tranche-turnover costs of about 0.65%/yr. Against a costless universe tranche book (a passive index proxy), honest P4+Q earns +0.10%/yr, t 0.19, with h2 -0.21. 'Edge over the universe survives' therefore depends on assuming the benchmark itself trades at institutional costs.

wave1.headline: Two new signals helped P4+Q before 2026: excluding names whose issuer just launched a new debenture offer (from the CVM offers registry), or whose sector's commodity nowcast is bad, added +0.34%/yr (t 2.9, both halves positive). But this combination was chosen after seeing the ICs, the Holm-adjusted p across all 20 variants tried is 0.064, and it did -0.09 vs P4+Q in the short 2026 holdout. It is a borderline candidate, not a proven improvement.
wave1.best: P4Q_ex_supply_or_nc_expo: P4+Q minus names whose issuer filed a debenture offer at CVM in the last 90 days, or whose sector's exposure-weighted commodity nowcast is below -1 (126-bday monthly tranches, 25 bps)
insights: Issuer's own recent debenture issuance (CVM offers registry, ICVM 400/476 plus RCVM 160, point-in-time by filing date) is the strongest new alternative signal. Within P4+Q, the IC on the 6-month forward return is -0.090 (NW t -4.8), and names flagged in the last 90 days underperform the rest of P4+Q by -1.68%/yr (t -2.5). Across the whole universe the effect is weak (-0.22%/yr).

The supply effect exists only outside regulated infrastructure. Excluding only non-infra issuers gives +0.21 vs P4+Q (t 2.2); excluding only infra issuers (power, sanitation, toll roads) gives -0.02. For concession companies and their project vehicles, repeat issuance is routine capex funding.

The gain grows with the look-back window: 30d +0.14, 60d +0.26, 90d +0.34, 180d +0.48 (62 names), 365d +0.63 (only 37 names). The event study backs this reading: across 850 offers, the issuer's existing bonds lose only -0.14% in the 63 days before and -0.30% in the 126 days after (about 0 after for P4+Q issuers). So it behaves like a 'frequent borrower / growing debt' quality signal, not short-term supply pressure. Shifting the offer dates by one year either way flips the effect to about -0.10.

Sector commodity nowcasts only matter among high-carry names. A 6-month commodity move below -1 standard deviation predicts -1.6%/yr for P4+Q names in exposed sectors (t -2.4 to -2.9), while the universe-wide IC is about 0. As an overlay alone it adds +0.09 (t 1.5), which beats every one of 20 placebos that reshuffle which nowcast goes with which sector (their p95 is +0.067).

The combined rule is robust across settings: +0.33 with weekly tranches, +0.40 at hold 63, +0.14 at hold 252, cohort 6m +0.43 (t 6.0), +0.31 at 50 bps, +0.32 in the rec40 recovery scenario. Leaving the 5 most-excluded issuers in the book still gives +0.28. Excluding the same number of random P4+Q names averages -0.03 (p95 +0.07). Max drawdown improves from -1.39 to -0.94.

Several signals came out null as overlays: rating and outlook changes (+0.00 to +0.03; too rare in P4+Q, and mostly already captured by the rich and quality filters), sector-level supply momentum (-0.05), ANEEL distribution tariff resets (+0.00), the hand-built margin nowcast alone (+0.02), and adding carry names with strong nowcasts (-0.01).
Sealed holdout (2026-01 to 2026-09, run once at the end): -0.09 vs P4+Q (t -0.7) and +3.25 vs the universe. Too short to confirm or refute.

The gain is highly concentrated. On a 6-month cohort attribution, the top 5 issuers supply about 81% of the benefit of the exclusion: Americanas 25%, Oncoclinicas 24%, Dasa 13%, and two wind SPVs about 18%. The Americanas collapse dominates. Americanas was in P4+Q on only 3 dates (2022-11 to 2023-01), and the supply leg flagged all 3 after its late-2022 debenture offer. January 2023 alone is +0.35pp, about 26% of the 4-year total. Excluding 2023, the gain falls to +0.24 (t 2.06). By year: 2022 +0.06, 2023 +0.63, 2024 +0.42, 2025 +0.23.

wave2.headline: On a rebuilt, never-used 2015–2020 debenture grid, frozen P4+Q beats the universe by +1.83%/yr (t 3.7). P7's extra edge shrinks to +0.12%/yr vs P4+Q (t 0.86, Holm p 1.0), a quarter of its in-sample size, and the factor_zoo screen turns negative (−0.35).
wave2.best: P7 as frozen (P4+Q minus the bottom 20% on equity health, carry weights, 5% issuer cap, R$500m liquidity cap), run out of sample on the rebuilt 2015-01..2020-12 grid. Monthly decisions, 126-bday tranches, 25 bps. Without the liquidity cap it gives +0.21 (t 1.43).
insights: The carry-selection core generalises out of sample. Over 72 never-seen months (2015-01..2020-12), P4+Q earns +2.75%/yr over CDI and beats the universe by +1.83%/yr (t 3.7), more than in-sample (+1.12). P4 beats U by +1.68 (t 3.5). A random-book placebo of the same size averages +1.03 (p95 +1.26) against P4+Q's +2.92.

The universe was a bad place in 2015–16. It earned only +0.33%/yr over CDI, while IDA-DI earned +1.15 and P4+Q beat U by +2.85%/yr (t 4.9). In 2020 the sign reverses: U beats P4+Q by +0.40, because high-carry names fell hardest in the COVID redemption crash (Mar–May 2020: P4+Q −3.4%, U −2.7%, IDA-DI −4.5%).

P7's edge over P4+Q keeps its sign but shrinks to a quarter of its in-sample size: +0.12 (t 0.86) out of sample vs +0.44 (t 2.6) in 2022–25. By period it is +0.20 in 2015–16, −0.07 in 2017–19 and +0.55 in 2020. A random-screen placebo averages +0.04 (p95 +0.105), so P7 sits just above it. Without the liquidity cap the edge is +0.21 (t 1.43), against +1.00 in-sample.

The equity-health screen carries P7's out-of-sample edge; carry weighting does not. The eqh screen alone gives +0.10 vs P4+Q, carry weights alone +0.02. The eqh score's 6m IC inside P4 is +0.135 (t 3.4, 33 dates), the only component with robust out-of-sample cross-sectional information. Carry's IC inside P4 is +0.18 (t 5.9), but equal-weight P4+Q already harvests it.

The Q screen keeps its sign but not its size. P4+Q − P4 is +0.15 (t 0.44) vs about +0.3 in 2022–25: +0.35 in 2015–16, −0.09 in 2017–19, +0.51 in 2020. The quality composite's IC inside P4 is actually negative (−0.11, t −2.6) and carry-neutral it is about 0, so 'drop the worst quintile' works only as a tail screen, not as a ranking.

The factor_zoo composite screen flips sign out of sample. It is −0.35%/yr vs P4+Q (t −1.42), negative in every sub-period (2015 −1.4). This supports the wave-1 finding that its +0.36 in 2022–25 came from dodging a few blow-ups.

The macro_cycle mom63 gate is drawdown insurance, confirmed on a new crisis. It sidestepped COVID: +3.0%/yr vs P4+Q in 2020, 2020 maxDD −0.6% vs −5.5%, Mar–May +0.5% vs −3.4%. It paid for that with −0.28 in 2015–16 and −0.54 in 2017–19 (whipsaws and switch costs), so net +0.14 (t 0.28). Across 2015–2025 it has helped in exactly two episodes, COVID and Americanas.

rec40 barely matters pre-2021: only 17 bonds stop trading below 0.90 in the rebuilt grid. The 2015–16 corporate defaults (Oi, Sete and others) were mostly not in the tradable, eligible SND universe, so the test covers a recession but few in-universe blow-ups.

problems: P7's +0.12%/yr edge over P4+Q is almost entirely 2020. It is +0.03%/yr (t 0.28) over 2015-2019, +0.10 (t 0.60) over 2016-2020 and +0.55 in 2020 alone. The claim that it 'keeps its sign' therefore rests on one crisis year, so the out-of-sample edge is effectively zero, not a quarter of the in-sample edge.

The P7 random-screen placebo in results.json used only 10 seeds, so its p95 is unreliable. In my 40 new seeds the mean was +0.03 and p95 +0.10, and 1 of 40 (2.5%) reached +0.12. P7 does sit around the placebo's 97th percentile, but that is one comparison inside a 7-variant family, and Holm p is 1.0 for every variant.
Carry weighting with the liquidity cap and no eqh screen gives -0.006 vs P4+Q. This supports the claim that carry weighting adds nothing out of sample.

wave2.headline: P7 is fragile rather than refuted. Its equity-health screen is not a placebo artefact: it is worth about +0.5%/yr over properly matched random drops and is even larger under honest costs. But it rests on about 10 issuers and 5 months, has an iid t of 1.7, and does not clear the t≈3.8 bar that a ~280–440-variant search requires. The realistic increment over P4+Q is about +0.25–0.35%/yr, not significant.
wave2.best: P7 as published: P4+Q minus the universe-listed bottom-20% EQH composite (eq_dd252, -eq_vol63, eq_r126), weighted by carry with a liquidity cap at R$500m and an issuer cap of 5%. The pre-declared flag-vote variant FV2 (drop names with 2 or more of the EQH, zoo, NegEvents and supply flags, same construction) was +0.60 (t 4.1) vs P4+Q, but only +0.10 (t 1.3) vs P7.
insights: P7's own placebo was contaminated. On average 40% of its 'random' listed drops were the EQH-flagged names themselves. Fine carry-decile × sector strata make it worse: 94–97% overlap, placebo mean +0.43, which would falsely refute P7. Zero-overlap controls (drop the same number of comparable NON-flagged listed names, same carry/liquidity construction) average -0.05 to +0.01 vs P4+Q. The 'mechanical +0.16 from dropping listed names' is therefore not real, and the placebo-adjusted screen alpha is +0.49 to +0.55 (NW t 2.3–2.4), not +0.3.

The NW t of 3.29 is flattered by a lag-2 autocorrelation of -0.47 in the monthly P7−P4+Q series, which makes the Newey-West variance smaller than the iid variance. The iid t is 1.72. The series is fat-tailed (skew 2.2, kurtosis 10.8, median month +0.02%), and the 5%-winsorised diff is +0.34 (t 1.83).

Concentration: the top 1/3/5/10 issuers account for 19/43/62/94% of the cohort gain, led by Oncoclínicas and Americanas. Dropping the top-10 issuers from both books leaves +0.10 (t 0.9). Excluding the top 3 months leaves +0.09 and the top 5 leaves 0.00. Leave-one-month-out ranges from +0.31 to +0.57, and leave-one-issuer-out (top 15 and bottom 5) from +0.39 to +0.59.

P7 is exactly additive. The EQH screen on EW P4+Q adds +0.38 (t 2.1) and the carry/liquidity construction +0.19 (t 1.5), with an interaction of -0.06. Regressing the P7 diff on the two single-component books gives betas of 1.01 and 1.00, R² 0.93 and alpha -0.07.

The construction leg is portfolio_construction's result. P7 is -0.07 vs PC's recommended mv_emp_g20_fund500m, and -0.07 vs PC top-25-carry@R$500m with the EQH screen bolted on. P7 is +0.29 (t 1.2) vs PC top-25@500m without the screen. The only new content is the EQH screen.

Multiplicity: 277 variants excluding bias_audit, 439 including it (counted from 16 results.json). Bonferroni/Holm 5% needs |t| of 3.74 or 3.86; at N=277–439, P7's p comes out at 0.28–0.44. The deflated Sharpe is 0.07 at N=277 and 0.05 at N=439.

The screen is stable across specifications. EQH q=0.1/0.2/0.3 gives +0.45/+0.50/+0.48. Single components give eq_dd252 +0.47, eq_r126 +0.42, eq_vol63 +0.35 (all t ≥ 2). A fundamentals lag of 60/90/120d on Q in both books gives +0.49/+0.49/+0.52; the lag hurts P4+Q itself (-0.04/-0.07/-0.14), not the increment.

Under honest assumptions (liquidity-bucket costs, harsh survivorship, holiday-accrual fix, lag-90 Q) the edge grows to +0.68 (NW t 4.2, iid t 2.5). P7 is +1.51 over CDI vs +0.83 for P4+Q and +0.18 for U. Minus zero-overlap placebos it is +0.69 to +0.70. Part of this is by construction: EQH avoids names that later go silent at the assumed 40% recovery.

Pre-declared flag vote: FV2 carry is +0.60 (t 4.1, 50bps +0.58), FV3 carry +0.43, FV2 EW +0.48 and FV3 EW +0.27. vs P7, FV2 is +0.10 (t 1.3) and FV3 EW is -0.23 (t -2.1). Requiring 3 flags drops too few names (about 7 of 103) to matter. Two votes is the useful setting, but the gain over EQH alone is insignificant.
The recomputed 2026 holdout matches the published figure: P7 vs P4+Q is +0.68%/yr (t 2.25, 9 months).

problems: Wrong folder name in the task: 'research/nightly/w2_p7_adversarial_verification' does not exist. The work is in research/nightly/p7_adversarial_verification/, and its README is titled w2_p7_adversarial_verification.

The kurtosis figure does not reproduce exactly. I get an excess kurtosis of 8.8 (pandas) and a skew of 2.30; the README says 10.8 and 2.2. This is probably a difference in estimator definition, and it does not change the conclusion.

The README says negative autocorrelation 'flatters' the NW t (3.29). That framing is debatable. The negative lag-2 autocorrelation (-0.47) is real: large gain months partly reverse (for example Dec-2024 +0.78, then Jan and Feb 2025 at -0.19 and -0.25). When autocorrelation is negative, a lower long-run variance is legitimate. The real problem is that NW is unstable at n=48: the t is 1.74 at lag 0, 2.45 at lag 2, 3.29 at lag 6 and 4.02 at lag 12. The iid t of 1.72 is a conservative bound, not the 'true' t.

wave2.headline: A point-in-time 12-month distress-hazard model (AUC about 0.69, versus 0.66 for the spread level alone) does not improve on carry. Ranking on expected-loss carry loses to P4+Q, and a PD-quintile screen does worse than Q. On top of P7 it costs about 0.12%/yr and is no better than a random screen of the same size (placebo p 0.76). The model is under-identified: fewer than 30 hard-default issuer onsets in every year of 2021–25.
wave2.best: C_lgbm_P7+PDq: P7 (combined/p7.py make_signal) with issuers in the universe-top-quintile of walk-forward monotone-LightGBM 12m distress PD removed from its p4q base. It is +0.38%/yr vs P4+Q, but that comes entirely from P7: vs P7 it is -0.12 (t -1.0).
insights: Model quality: pooled out-of-sample AUC on debenture issuers is 0.655 (logit) and 0.686 (LGBM). Spread level alone scores 0.658, the past-event flag 0.61 and ND/EBITDA 0.61. By year, LGBM scores 0.67 / 0.66 / 0.66 / 0.81 / 0.85 for 2021–25 (2025 censored at 2025-12-31). On 'clean' issuer-months with no event in the prior year it is only 0.60, so much of the AUC is persistence of distress.

Coverage: pooled LGBM AUC is 0.69 for listed issuers (0.89–0.92 in 2024–25) and 0.67 for unlisted ones. Issuers with no fundamentals (unregistered SPVs) score 0.63, and only 0.50–0.60 in 2021–23. Fundamentals do not close the unlisted gap.

Under-identified: hard-event onsets among debenture issuers are 1 / 2 / 14 / 10 / 10 for 2021–25 (bias_audit distress, severe rating actions, CVM RJ/default filings). Adding bond-loss episodes gives 7 / 11 / 46 / 23 / 34. The PD is therefore mostly a detector of soft mark drawdowns and of RJ persistence.

The PD model sees the events but not the losses. Inside P4, the LGBM PD flag catches 37% of issuer-months with an event in the next 12m at a 16% flag rate, about the same as Q (38% at 18%) and the P7 equity-health screen (36% at 15%). But flagged names still earn +0.66% over the next 6 months, versus +0.40% for Q-flagged and -0.44% for equity-flagged names. PD catches the soft episodes that recover and misses the hard blow-ups.

Expected-loss carry is a worse ranking variable than raw carry. PD is nearly orthogonal to carry (Spearman -0.01 logit, +0.10 LGBM). IC vs fwd_126 drops from 0.25 for carry to 0.09–0.12 for EL-carry, and -PD alone has IC of about 0. The A books lose 0.25–0.33%/yr to P4+Q, including -0.9 to -1.0%/yr in 2022–23. LGD 0.4 vs 0.6 barely matters.

The PD quintile screen is weaker than Q. P4 minus the PD quintile scores -0.11 (LGBM) and -0.25 (logit) vs P4+Q; it adds only +0.08 to +0.22 over P4, against about +0.33 for Q. P4+Q minus the PD quintile adds +0.04 / +0.09 (t <= 0.55).

On top of P7 the PD screen hurts. It is -0.12 (LGBM) and -0.15 (logit) vs P7, negative in both halves (-0.20 / -0.03), at 50 bps (-0.13) and under harsh survivorship (+0.68 vs +0.76 for P7 alone). A random screen dropping the same number of names averages -0.08 (p95 +0.04), so the placebo p is 0.76.

New public data: CVM IPE 2019–26 RJ / default filings for all CVM issuers, after a counterparty-mention filter that removes Vale, Klabin, Engie, Natura and others that only mentioned someone else's RJ. Plus CVM fundamentals for all 933 filers, which gives pre-2021 training labels. The broad panel's AUC of 0.93 is RJ persistence, not prediction.

Bond-loss labels need care by kind. A -10% rate-hedged drawdown flags 220 IPCA issuers, and only 10% of them have any hard event (rate-hedge noise), vs 62% for DI+ floaters. IPCA/PRE therefore use a -20% market-neutral threshold.

Sealed holdout (2026-01 to 2026-09, read once, frozen C_lgbm): +1.11 vs P4+Q (t 2.9) against +0.68 for P7 alone, so the screen added about +0.43, the opposite sign to pre-2026. That is 9 months and one episode; the holdout PDs had learned the 2025 events (Ambipar, Braskem, Oncoclinicas). It is the only hint the model improves as labels accumulate, and it does not change the verdict.

problems: Look-ahead in event features. In build_data.ipe_events, the counterparty filter keeps a Fato Relevante when the issuer's own RJ document falls within ±400 days of it, and that window includes FUTURE documents. 10 of 316 facts, at 8 issuers, are kept only because of an RJ document that came later. These events feed ev_past365 and ev_days_since, and ev_days_since is the top LGBM gain feature. This leak favours the PD model, so it does not weaken the negative verdict. It does make the AUC figures (0.686 and the 0.81–0.85 for 2024–25) slightly optimistic.

The IPCA/PRE bond-loss threshold was moved from -10% to -20% after looking at how often it overlapped with hard events. bond_loss_events uses the full path including 2026 (load_panel holdout=True, _Rmat). That is a label-definition choice made partly with holdout-period data. It is disclosed but not isolated.
The placebo uses only 20 random draws, so p = 0.76 is coarse, with a minimum attainable p of about 0.048. The qualitative conclusion is unaffected.

wave2.headline: Extending the screen to unlisted issuers adds nothing detectable to P7. 64% of P7's weight has no equity series, CVM FRE parent mapping recovers only 2.5% of rows, and proxy screens beat P4+Q only as much as P7 already does (+0.02 to +0.13%/yr vs P7, t ≤ 0.9). About half of the unlisted names' outperformance disappears under harsh survivorship plus realistic liquidity costs.
wave2.best: X3_sector_proxy (picked by the pre-set rule, highest t vs P4+Q): P7, with EQH (the equity-health composite) pooled over own equity plus FRE/name parent equity, and for unlisted names with no parent the bottom 20% of a listed sector-peer equity composite dropped. It beats P4+Q by +0.52%/yr (t 4.1), but that is P7's edge: vs P7 it adds only +0.02 (t 0.13). X6_cascade adds the most vs P7: +0.13 (t 0.88).
insights: Coverage gap: before 2026, 66% of universe rows have own or harness-parent equity, but only 43% of P4+Q rows and 33% of P7's weight do. 64% of P7's weight is never screened. It sits in 343 truly unlisted issuers such as Aegea, Cagece, BRK, Iguá, Metrô SP, Solví, V2i and Transbrasiliana.

Parent mapping has a low ceiling. PIT CVM FRE control edges (participacao_sociedade and posicao_acionaria, ≥50% control, dated by DT_RECEB) map 100 issuers, but that is only +2.5% of rows (3.6% of P7's weight), mostly transmission, wind and toll SPEs of Alupar, EDP, Equatorial, ISA, Auren and Motiva. Listed parents outside the 161 series would add only about 4% of unlisted rows. Name-token matching had 45% precision (10 of 22) and added 0 priced rows.

The sector-peer equity composite is a good stand-in for true equity health on listed names (Spearman 0.66; its bottom-20% flag hits the true EQH bottom quintile 63% of the time vs 20% at random). The bond-mark proxy is not (Spearman −0.02, precision 0.26). The fundamentals proxy adds nothing because the Q filter already removes every name it would flag (X4 is identical to X1).
P7's EQH composite has no rank IC (+0.012, t 0.3 on listed rows). The screen works only through tail and blow-up avoidance, which is why proxies with decent correlation still add little.

vs P7, with 5 extensions and Holm p = 1 for all: parent equity +0.07 (t 0.72); sector proxy +0.02 (t 0.13); bond proxy +0.07; cascade +0.13 (t 0.88), still +0.12 under harsh survivorship plus liquidity costs. The cascade beats a matched random drop of unscreened names (placebo mean 0.00, p95 +0.06), but it is not significant against P7.

Unlisted minus listed in the universe is +0.89%/yr (t 1.97) at base. It falls to +0.69 under harsh survivorship, +0.66 under liquidity-bucket costs, and +0.46 (t 1.1) with both. All of it comes from 2024–25 (2022–23 is −0.24 under both). Unlisted rows are 2.8x more likely to belong to bonds that later go silent below 0.98 (1.86% vs 0.67%), trade less (41 vs 53 trades in 30 days) and carry more (141 vs 104 bps). Within carry deciles the gap is +0.78%/yr (t 1.8).

Fund_flows' universe 'orphan' premium (+0.47) turns negative under realistic costs (−0.40, −0.27 with harsh survivorship too), so it is a cost and stale-mark artefact. Inside P4+Q, orphans stay ahead (+1.5, t 1.8), but that is about 9% of the book and a few names.

In the sealed 2026 holdout (read once): P7 is +0.68 vs P4+Q; X3 is +0.84 vs P4+Q (+0.16 vs P7, t 1.2); X6 is +0.79 (+0.11 vs P7, t 0.3). Unlisted beat listed inside P4+Q by +1.99%/yr (t 2.2), because listed names were hit harder in 2026.

problems: X3_sector_proxy, the variant labelled 'best', does not beat its own placebo. Randomly dropping the same number of unscreened P4+Q names gives p = 0.10 (actual +0.021 vs P7; placebo mean -0.044, p95 +0.040). Its +0.52%/yr vs P4+Q (t 4.1) is P7's edge, and the sector-proxy flags add nothing beyond random dropping. The README says so, but the 'best' framing and the headline t of 4.1 overstate the variant.

The pre-set selection rule (highest t vs P4+Q) does not fit the question, which is whether the extension adds to P7. It picked X3, whose gain vs P7 is about zero (+0.02, t 0.13; excluding the 3 best months, -0.14). The only variant whose flags beat the random-drop placebo is X6_cascade (+0.125 vs P7, placebo p95 +0.06, 20 draws), and it is still not significant vs P7 (t 0.88, Holm p 1).

X4_fund_proxy is identical to X1. I confirmed it: the px_fund bottom-20% flags 1,670 rows and 0 of them are in P4+Q. So only 4 distinct extensions exist, yet Holm counts 5 variants plus P7 and P4 as rows. Holm p is 1 for all of them anyway, so nothing changes.

wave2.headline: Brazilian debentures in 2021–25 came with no new-issue concession: new series priced 16 bps inside the issuer's own curve, and the first print sits at the issue price. A primary sleeve of wide new issues (A2) shows +1.31%/yr vs P4+Q, but it is not significant across 30 variants (global Holm p 0.067). Half of it is carry, and it swings from −0.3 to +1.8 depending on how the 69% of bonds that never trade are marked.
wave2.best: A2_prim_conc50_scr: buys new debenture series at par (the bookbuilding / SND contract rate) at settlement when the concession is above 50 bps. The concession is the issue spread (CDI+ equivalent) minus the same-day peer-curve fair value, adjusted by the issuer's curve where the issuer has fresh bonds. The issuer must also pass P4's press screen, the P4+Q worst-quintile quality screen and P7's EQH bottom-20% screen. Each bond is held 126 bdays, bonds that never trade are marked to the peer-curve model, entry costs nothing and the exit costs 25 bps/2.
insights: There is no average new-issue concession. Across 3,566 series settling 2021-06 to 2025, new issues priced 16 bps INSIDE the issuer's outstanding curve (median -9, t -4.0, n=1,331). The first SND print sits exactly at the issue spread (median move 0.0 bps) and is on average 5.7 bps wider (t 2.5). Unlike US IG, issuers in the 2021–25 inflow boom priced flat.

The 'concession' vs the peer curve (+36 bps mean, +22 median) is a carry and credit proxy. In month-clustered regressions controlling for the issue spread, it predicts neither the first-print move (t -0.9) nor the 126-bday return vs peers (t 0.0). The primary-buyer return vs peers rises steeply across concession quintiles (-2.18, -0.28, -0.14, +1.37, +2.00% over 126 bdays), but the mean issue spread rises from 65 to 384 bps along with it.

An allocation at the bookbuilding rate is worth nothing extra. The same selection bought at the first print does as well: A1 minus B1 is -0.37%/yr (t -0.5). A primary buyer at par earns +0.11% vs the peer cohort over 126 bdays (t 0.3).

There is a real but small seasoning drift. Bonds bought at the first print beat their peer cohort by +0.42% over 126 bdays (month-clustered t 5.0). It is +1.16 for Lei 12.431, +1.13 for IPCA, +0.02 for DI+, +0.97 for first-time vs +0.28 for repeat issuers. In the harness, a book of names first printed within the last 31 days is only +0.02 vs U and -1.10 vs P4+Q (cohort +0.45%/yr, t 2.2). P4+Q minus new issues is +0.07: the drift cannot be harvested in the secondary book.

Only 56% of new series ever print on SND, with a median of 23 bdays from settlement to first print; only 27% print within 21 bdays. Among A2's wide issues, 69% never print within the hold. The primary-sleeve result therefore depends on marking: A2 vs P4+Q is +1.31 with model marks, -0.29 with never-printed bonds at cash and +1.79 at par plus carry. Any primary-alpha claim must state its marking convention.

A2 (primary, concession > 50, screens) is +1.31%/yr vs P4+Q (NW t 2.98). The halves are +0.96 (2022–23) and +1.67 (2024–25); 50 bps gives +1.45, rec40 +1.35, vs P7 +0.81 (t 1.6), and excluding the top-10 issuers +1.33. About half is carry: P4+Q restricted to spreads of at least 260 bps (A2's median issue spread) earns +0.74 (t 3.5). Spread-matched random new issues earn +0.59 (p95 +0.91).

Every new issue bought blindly (A0) loses -1.39%/yr vs P4+Q (t -2.5). Random new issues, the placebo with the same count per month as A1, lose -1.47 (p95 -1.07). Being in the primary market is not an edge in itself; selection by carry is.
Realistic sizing makes it immaterial. P4+Q with a 20% A2 sleeve adds +0.27%/yr (t 2.98) at a 100% fill and only +0.08 at a 30% fill (+0.09 at 50 bps).

Sealed 2026 holdout (9 months, read once): A2 is +2.49%/yr vs P4+Q (t 4.1), and +1.48 (t 2.3) even with never-printed bonds at cash. The blend adds +0.50, P7 +0.68, and the harness all-new-issues book -2.41. In the 2026 redemption wave, bonds issued in the last 6 months held up while the seasoned book did not, consistent with a low early default hazard. It is one episode, and part of it is still model-marked.

2024 was the tight-pricing year. The average concession was 8 bps, the first print was 24 bps wider than issue, and primary buyers lost 1.12% vs peers. ICVM 400 deals (26) were the worst, at -6.4% vs peers; the RCVM 160 automatic rite was mildly positive (+0.37).

caveats: Assuming a fill at the bookbuilding (SND contract) rate on every selected deal is optimistic. Hot deals are scaled back and cold deals are filled in full. The 30% fill blend is only a crude haircut, and the primary entry was charged no cost.

44% of all new series, and 69% of A2's, never print within the hold. These are marked to model (carry minus duration times the change in the peer-bucket median spread), so their credit events stay invisible. This is the stale-mark and survivorship zone, and the result ranges from -0.29 (cash) to +1.79 (par plus carry).

Settlement is proxied by the registry's accrual start ('Inicio da Rentabilidade'). The fair value and curves are taken on the grid day before it, while the true bookbuilding happens a few days earlier. The contract rate is today's registry rate, which could reflect repactuation for a few series. 12 series that traded before the proxy settlement date were dropped.

Concession thresholds (0/50 bps) were set after the pre-2026 event study, which is in-sample. A2 has global Holm p 0.067 across 30 variants; within the 11-variant portfolio family alone it would be 0.031.

problems: Mild look-ahead in dur_iss. The duration factor is dur_fp/T_fp, taken from the bond's FIRST SND print, which comes after settlement. It feeds the IPCA/PRE issue-spread conversion, the peer fair-value interpolation (so conc) and the dur x d(peer spread) model mark. Using the default factor for every bond barely changes the selection (1053 of 1064 series in common). But A2 vs P4+Q under the author's model marks falls from +1.31 (t 2.98) to +1.02 (t 1.87, p 0.06). The model-marked leg is sensitive to the duration assumption.
The eligibility filter drops 12 series that traded before their registry settlement date. This uses post-decision information, but the effect is negligible.
The model mark for never-printed bonds uses the peer-bucket spread change lagged one day (sp[start-1:e] diffs). The timing is off by one day. It is not a leak.

combined.headline: P7 beats P4+Q by +0.50%/yr before 2026 (NW t 3.3, Holm p 0.01; +0.47 with realistic costs) and by +0.68%/yr in the sealed 2026 holdout (t 2.2). P7 is P4+Q minus the worst equity-health quintile, weighted by carry, with a liquidity cap for an R$500m fund. The gain comes mostly from avoiding a few blow-ups: without the 3 best months it drops to +0.09.
combined.best: P7 (pre-registered). Candidates are P4+Q. Drop P4+Q names in the universe-listed bottom 20% of an equity-health composite: the mean percentile of eq_dd252 (+), -eq_vol63 and eq_r126 (+); unlisted names are kept. Weights are proportional to cdi_bps, with a 5% issuer cap and a cap per position of 25% of 91-day SND volume at R$500m. No timing overlay or hedge. Monthly decisions, 126-bday tranches, 25 bps.
insights: The wave-1 avoid signals largely capture the same thing. On P4+Q rows the Jaccard overlaps of the dropped sets are: equity-health/zoo 0.29, equity-health/events 0.26, events/supply 0.19. Names flagged by only one signal do not underperform (6-month return relative to P4+Q of -0.02 to +0.33%), while names flagged by 3 or more signals underperform by -1.36%. Adding every flag (V6) removes 33% of the book and does 0.14%/yr worse than P7.

The screen and the construction do different jobs, and together they give +0.50. The equity-health screen alone gives +0.38 (t 2.1) and cuts maxDD from -1.39 to -0.70. The carry and liquidity construction alone gives +0.19. Ablations vs P7: no screen -0.32, EW instead of the carry tilt -0.22 (t -3.1), no Q filter -0.10.

The liquidity cap costs about 0.43%/yr: the uncapped carry version gets +0.93 vs P4+Q. In exchange, the share of weight above the R$500m liquidity limit falls from 17% (P4+Q) and 28% (uncapped) to 0.3%. Capacity decays slowly: +0.56 at R$100m, +0.50 at R$500m, +0.35 at R$1bn, +0.34 at R$2bn.

Under honest assumptions (bias_audit liquidity-bucket costs plus harsh survivorship, where every stopped bond below 0.98 goes to 40%), levels fall: P7 +1.77%/yr over CDI, P4+Q +1.04, universe +0.32. The gap vs P4+Q widens to +0.73 (t 3.4), because P7 avoids more of the bonds that later go silent.
Timing and hedging still subtract even inside the combined book. The IDA-DI mom63 entry gate costs 0.39 and the Ibov-slump entry gate costs 0.23 (t -2.5), although both reduce drawdown.

A placebo that drops the same number of listed P4+Q names at random, with the same construction, gives a mean of +0.16 and a p95 of +0.25, against +0.50 actual. Part of any listed-name exclusion gain is a mechanical tilt toward unlisted names.

The gain is fragile. By year it is 2022 +0.09, 2023 +0.66, 2024 +1.19, 2025 +0.07. Excluding the best 3 months (2024-12, 2025-04, 2023-01) leaves +0.09 (t 0.46). Dropping the top-5 or top-10 contributing issuers from both books leaves +0.24 (t 2.3) and +0.10 (t 0.9).

Sealed holdout (2026-01..09, run once): P7 +0.76%/yr over CDI, P4+Q +0.08, P4 -0.73, universe -3.26, IDA-DI +0.53. P7 vs P4+Q is +0.68 (t 2.2), +0.65 at 50 bps and +0.60 with liquidity-bucket costs, positive in 6 of 9 months, with maxDD -0.67.

caveats: The components were chosen after reading wave-1 results on the same 2022-25 sample, so the Holm p of 0.01 over 12 rows understates the real search (more than 300 variants in wave 1). The 9-month holdout is the only clean test.
The edge is concentrated in a few blow-up avoidances in 2023-24. Without the 3 best months the gain is +0.09 (t 0.46); without the top-10 contributing issuers it is +0.10.
Smooth, stale, survivorship-biased marks inflate t and Sharpe. The harness also has a holiday-accrual bug worth about -0.13%/yr on levels (bias_audit).

The screen only sees listed issuers (about 41% of P4+Q). The unlisted tail is unscreened, and removing listed names mechanically tilts the book toward the unlisted zone where the survivorship bias lives.
